"Both protection coupons and protective tents have level restrictions. The cheapest ones can resist attacks below level 20, and the higher the level of resistance, the more expensive they get."

"That's a nice feature, very suitable for ensuring safety during wild outdoor travels."

Shang Feifan was tempted, but after checking the price of a protective tent, he realized it was beyond what he could currently afford. Therefore, he simply traded two sickles with a player for an ordinary, player-made tent.

Protection coupons were much cheaper than tents, and their shielding range was quite decent. They had a duration of one hundred hours—activated when needed and stowed away when not, making them extremely convenient. However, the price was still not cheap; a single protection coupon capable of resisting attacks below level 20 cost ten silver dahlus.

Shang Feifan calculated his remaining funds and regretfully found that he still couldn't afford one.

"In the early stages of the game, only by forming clans, guilds, or other organizations and pooling everyone's funds can people afford to buy these items with special buffs," Shang Feifan sighed. But he had no desire to form a clan, nor did he want to join any other players' organizations.

"Yeah, that's why many players are forming sworn brotherhoods right now, chipping in together to buy items with special effects, and heading out into the wild to slay monsters and do quests together. That's the method they use to accelerate their leveling." Fu Xiangjun had joined a guild established by first-phase players and was even one of the founding members—which was precisely why he had been able to earn one hundred silver so quickly.

"Right, haven't you noticed that the game planners seem somewhat reluctant to let players run outside?" Shang Feifan suddenly asked.

Fu Xiangjun nodded. "Not only do they not want players running all over the place, but they also use the minimum level requirements for unlocking class skills and talent skills to fence players in, forcing them to frantically grind various quests inside the camp until they reach the minimum level.

Still, this kind of 'guiding' approach is very common in games, mostly meant to let players quickly familiarize themselves with game mechanics. In this case, it probably also carries the intention of letting players hunker down and develop safely in the newbie village for a bit.

Of course, the more likely reason is that the game map hasn't been fully developed yet, and it's not yet suitable for players to go out exploring and adventuring."

Shang Feifan said, "But there are still a few people who love adventure and freedom and run outside anyway."

Fu Xiangjun replied, "The outside world is dangerous. People who run out without an organization are very likely to get killed right back to their respawn points. After a few attempts, not many players dare to run around recklessly anymore. Like our Second Camp that we're developing right now, it was only because the Valley Master issued an order, led by NPCs, that we were able to arrive smoothly and stake our claim."

Thinking of Moyue Valley Town, Shang Feifan wondered if that place might be the next game newbie village, and whether he had somehow exploited a bug to arrive there ahead of time?

Fu Xiangjun, being an average gaming young man, commented quite objectively at this moment: "As long as the vast majority of people can be kept in the newbie village camp, data balance can be maintained. The few who run out won't have any impact on the overall game anyway; finding a high-level wild boss is enough to send any wandering players packing back to their spawn points."

Seeing that Shang Feifan remained silent, Fu Xiangjun asked curiously, "What are you thinking about?"

Shang Feifan was currently contemplating whether, if he stubbornly insisted on bringing A-Dai toward Moyue Valley Town, he would end up being killed by a wild boss along the way.

"Actually, you could stay behind to do some quests first. Once you reach level 10 and have basic self-preservation capabilities, it won't be too late to go on your quest to help A-Dai find his father," Fu Xiangjun suggested, not sounding particularly tactful.

Shang Feifan shook his head and stubborn as iron, replied, "I'm not staying.正好正好 (might as well) test just how large of a map this game world has actually rendered."

Besides, he still had a quest on him for exploring a new world map record, and he also wanted to use this opportunity to earn a few more contribution points.

He had a gut feeling that contribution points would be far more useful than currency.

That night, the two of them rented two beds in an inn for two copper dahus.

The most common setup in the inn was a large open-dormitory room, where fifty beds were packed densely together. The players didn't mind this at all; after all, they weren't really sleeping here—they were simply storing their bodies and valuables here before logging off.

In the real world.

Shang Feifan took off his helmet, sat up, stretched his limbs, and raised an eyebrow slightly.

That sensation of a warm current flowing through his body had returned.

Sitting on the couch with a helmet on for so long—even on a couch—his body should have felt stiff.

Yet, with just a slight stretch, his body and limbs felt as limber as if he had just finished a warm-up exercise, and his energy was exceptionally vibrant.

Over on his side, Fu Xiangjun also took off his helmet.

Shang Feifan headed to the kitchen for a glass of water, and passing by Fu Xiangjun, asked offhandedly, "Feeling terrible?"

Fu Xiangjun stretched his limbs and neck, making a series of cracking sounds. "Sitting for so long, how could I not feel terrible? I feel like my whole body has turned to stone."

"Tired? Sleepy?"

Fu Xiangjun shook his head. "Tired isn't the word, and I'm not sleepy either. It just feels like I woke up from a really long dream."

That dreamlike sensation upon waking, coupled with the greatly dampened pain sensation in the game, were the boundary lines established by game developers to let players distinguish between reality and the game. The dreamlike quality also minimized psychological and mental trauma to the players to the greatest extent possible.

It was much like slaughtering everything in your path or committing all sorts of evil deeds in a dream; once you woke up, you were still you, and the dream would not affect your real life, let alone trigger any cascading reactions.

"What about you?" Fu Xiangjun stood up and gave a massive stretch.

Shang Feifan walked into the kitchen. "Same."

*No,* he didn't feel like it was a dream at all. Even the pain he experienced was one hundred percent real.

While the pain sensation could be adjusted by players themselves—the laptop system allowed dialing it down to a maximum of fifty percent—Shang Feifan had checked his neural-link system panel, and his pain setting had been at one hundred percent from the very beginning. He had no intention of adjusting it for the time being.

chunks.chineseText:
第22章 虎不帅现状

次日一大早，商非凡带着阿呆、背着行李包，走出营地，一直用脚走到看不到玩家和营地的地方，才用口哨召唤来狰爷，跳上狰爷的背。

伏向军没和他同行，就好像两人只是两个没有关系的陌生玩家，昨天只是临时搭伙做生意，今天就分道扬镳。

就在老商骑着巨蟹虫、带着崽儿向莫约山谷而去时，遥远的莫约山谷镇迎来了一群不速之客。

虎不帅知道这些人是为何而来。

就是为他。

王都很多人不想他回去，但也有些人渴望他回去。

不想他回去的人分成两拨。

一拨尊重他的想法，希望他能安稳生活，不要被搅入王继承权的乱局中，希望他能离开王都越远越好。

另一拨不想他留在王都的人则是怕他抢占他们的利益和权力、怕他得到王的重视和更多来自王的父爱。

渴望他回去的人同样分成两拨。

一拨希望他能留在王都，好方便他们把水搅得更混。

另一拨则希望他能留在王都继续当挡箭牌和替死鬼。

这次来的一拨人就是希望他回到王都给某人继续当挡箭牌和替死鬼的。

可他之前已经差点死过一次。

实际上，他这具身体在五年前就已经真实死亡过。

五年前，他突然在这具身体上醒来，发现自己再次魂穿。

他不知道自己为何会再次魂穿，只知道自己濒临死亡时似乎听到了有人在呼唤。

他被呼唤声吸引，当他凝神细听时，就觉得一阵昏眩，再醒来就是在这具新身体中。

第二次魂穿！

如果不是第一次魂穿的经历让他认识到自己仍旧是那个普通平凡的自己，他都要再次以为他是老天爷钟爱的命运之子了。

说实话，郎沐宁可自己死得干干净净、不留任何痕迹。

如果能转世重生，他也希望不带任何记忆的重生。

他并不厌恶他的前两生，只是觉得没什么好回忆的。

就像一杯白开水，喝完就喝完，完全没必要回味。

但真的带着记忆再次魂穿，他也不会想要放弃这段生命。

他最大的优点也可能是缺点？

就是随波逐流。

像他这样的人，就像一根野草，也许不起眼，但到什么地方，稍微给点水土空气，就能扎根活下来。

第二次魂穿前，他在一座不算很出名的魔法学校当老师。

平时就带带低年级的孩子，给他们启蒙魔法知识和一些生活常识。

生活平淡，贵在安稳。

他带的孩子也都挺喜欢他的，他也喜欢和这些小不点相处。

他死的时候，那所魔法学校所在的国家发生了战争。

学校的老师都在设法保护学生撤离。

他没有家累，自愿留在最后，然后……敌人来袭，他选择自爆。

哪怕到现在他也并不后悔这一决定，甚至觉得自己也算死得其所，至少他保护了很多孩子，为他们拖延到足够的宝贵的撤离时间。

那时他是真的没有想到他的人生还能继续下去。

他听到那隐约的呼唤时，只以为是死亡时产生的幻觉，毕竟那时候他整个人都炸没了。

谁想，他竟然又活了。

后来根据他的观察和掌握的一些线索，他推测召唤他魂魄的人很可能就是原身母亲。

这点从原身母亲对他的态度上也能看出来，虽然直到原身母亲死亡那天，他们都没有戳破这个彼此都心知肚明的事实。

而他也默认了接过原身的身份和缠绕在原身身上的所有恩怨纠缠，并在原身母亲死亡那天，答应了她三个请求。

虽然不是他主动魂穿到这具身体上，但怎么说召唤他的人也给了他新的人生，这就像所有刚出生的孩子都没有选择权一样。

何况原身母亲在病死之前，悉心教导了他很多知识，他就当自己在偿还这份教导之情。

总之，郎沐很快就接受了他的第三次人生。不过他衷心希望这是最后一次“奇迹”，他不想再带着记忆魂穿了。

也许有人会渴望这种不可思议的奇迹，但他不想要。

跟不太成功的两段人生经历无关，他就是觉得一个人的人生该有始有终。

话说回头。

原身母亲在一年前“病”死，原身在五年前真正死掉，魂穿来的他在半年前也差点被原身儿时好友害死。

三条命！

他认为，不管原身母亲欠某些人多少人情，也都该还完了。

正好半年前他这具身体已经满二十岁，满足了他答应原身母亲的三个请求之一“未满二十岁以前不能离开王都，满二十岁以后随便去哪里”的条件，他就和名义上是他生身父亲的王深谈了一次，最后以养病的名义离开了王都。

他以为这就已经表明了他的态度，而王也没有阻止。

可某些人贪心不止，竟然又追了过来。

“拉斐尔！我终于找到你了。”

一行年轻兽人中的一个，一看到他，就激动地冲过来。

虎不帅面无表情地往旁边横走两步。

来人张开的双臂抱了个空，还踉跄了一下，等站稳身体，就一脸受伤地转头看向虎不帅。

“拉斐尔郎沐，你怎么能这样对我？你知道我这一路过来有多辛苦吗？”来人伤心欲绝地控诉。

虎不帅抱着一个瓦罐，回了一个字：“哦。”

“哦？这个哦是什么意思？你看到我就一点也不高兴吗？”来人生气。

虎不帅特别诚实地：“不高兴。”

来人英俊的脸庞皱成了包子褶，肩膀也塌了下来：“拉斐尔，你变了。”

虎不帅：“我一直都这样。”

“拉斐尔，你是不是还在怪我？那天我真的不知道……”

“够了！伊克斯泥奏凯！你这样对拉斐尔没用，他不吃你这一套。”一个个头高大、身上肌肉特别结实的有角兽人走过来，把伊克斯推到一边。

“兄弟，好久不见。”有角兽人只伸出拳头。

虎不帅也伸出拳头和对方碰了一下。

后面几个年轻兽人也一一过来和虎不帅打招呼。

虎不帅对他们不冷不淡地点头。

几个人和虎不帅都认识，知道他不是不欢迎他们，只是性格如此。

“我们到一边说话。”有角兽人带头走到一边。

他们一行人连带他们的坐骑已经堵住了小镇主干道，惹来不少人注目。

虎不帅面对有角兽人，神色有了一些温度：“好久不见，角马。”

角马干咳一声，压低声音：“我就直接跟你说正事了。我们这次过来除了想要解开你和伊克斯之间的误会，另外就是希望你能跟我们一起回去王都。”

虎不帅神色不动：“谁想让我回王都？”

角马没能推开硬要偷听的伊克斯，翻了个白眼，对虎不帅说：“除了我们的头，还有谁？你走了以后，他就像是断了一条胳膊，脾气都变得暴躁许多，尤其最近事情还多。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 22: The Current Predicament of Handsome Tiger (Part 1)

Early the next morning, Shang Feifan led A-Dai, carrying their luggage packs as they walked out of the camp. They kept walking on foot until the players and the camp were completely out of sight. Only then did he use a whistle to summon the Fierce Beast, leaping onto its back.

Fu Xiangjun did not travel with him. It was as if the two of them were completely unrelated, ordinary players who had merely teamed up temporarily for business yesterday and parted ways today.

Just as Old Shang rode his Giant Crab Worm alongside his little one, heading toward the Moyue Valley, a group of uninvited guests had arrived at the distant town nestled within the Moyue Valley.

Handsome Tiger knew why these people had come.

They were here for him.

Many people in the Royal Capital did not want him to return, but there were also those who desperately desired his return.

Those who did not want him to return were divided into two factions.

One faction respected his wishes, hoping he could live a stable life, far away from the chaotic struggles for the royal succession, and wishing for him to leave the Royal Capital as far as possible.

The other faction opposed his stay out of fear that he would encroach upon their interests and power, or that he would win the King's favor and receive a greater share of paternal affection.

Those who yearned for his return were likewise divided into two factions.

One faction hoped he would stay in the Royal Capital, making it easier for them to muddy the waters even further.

The other faction hoped he would remain in the Royal Capital to continue serving as a human shield and a scapegoat.

The group that had arrived this time belonged to the latter category—they wanted him to return to the Royal Capital to continue acting as a scapegoat and a shield for someone.

Yet, he had already nearly died once before.

In fact, this physical body of his had truly died five years ago.

Five years ago, he suddenly awoke within this body, realizing he had undergone soul-transmigration once again.

He had no idea why he had transmigrated a second time; he only knew that when he was on the brink of death, he seemed to hear someone calling out to him.

Attracted by the calling voice, as he concentrated to listen closely, a wave of dizziness washed over him, and when he woke up again, he was inside this new body.

His second soul-transmigration!

If not for the experience of his first transmigration reminding him that he was still just an ordinary, unremarkable person, he might have once again fancied himself a favored Child of Destiny chosen by the heavens.

To be honest, Lang Mu would rather have died completely and cleanly, leaving behind not a single trace.

If he could be reincarnated and reborn, he would have preferred it without any memories at all.

It wasn't that he loathed his previous two lives; he simply felt they were nothing worth reminiscing about.

Much like a glass of plain water—once you finished drinking it, there was no need to linger on the aftertaste.

Yet, having truly transmigrated once more with his memories intact, he had no intention of casting away this life either.

His greatest virtue, which might also be his flaw?

It was his ability to go with the flow.

A person like him was like a blade of wild grass—perhaps inconspicuous, but wherever he was taken, given just a tiny bit of soil, water, and air, he could strike root and survive.

Before his second soul-transmigration, he was a teacher at a rather obscure magic academy.

Normally, he taught the lower-grade children, initiating them into magical knowledge and basic common sense for daily life.

His life was plain, its greatest virtue being stability.

The children he taught all liked him very much, and he enjoyed spending time with these little ones.

When he died, a war had broken out in the country where that magic academy was located.

The teachers at the academy were all trying every means possible to protect the students during the evacuation.

He had no family encumbrances, so he volunteered to stay behind until the very end, and then… when the enemy attacked, he chose to detonate his own core.

Even now, he held no regrets regarding that decision; he even felt that his death had been meaningful—at least he had protected many children, buying them enough precious time to escape.

At the time, he genuinely never expected his life to continue.

When he heard that faint, distant calling, he simply assumed it was a hallucination produced at the moment of death, especially since his entire body had blown itself to smithereens.

Who would have thought that he would actually live again?

Later, based on his observations and the clues he had gathered, he deduced that the person who summoned his soul was most likely the original owner's mother.

This could also be discerned from the original owner's mother's attitude toward him, even though right up until the day she died, neither of them ever pierced the veil of that mutual, unspoken understanding.

He had also tacitly accepted taking over the original owner's identity along with all the entanglements of karma and grievances wrapped around him, and on the day the original owner's mother passed away, he promised her three requests.

Although he hadn't actively chosen to transmigrate into this body, the person who summoned him had, after all, granted him a new lease on life. It was much like how newborns have no say in their own birth.

Furthermore, before dying of illness, the original owner's mother had painstakingly taught him a vast amount of knowledge, so he simply treated it as repaying that debt of tutelage.

In any case, Lang Mu quickly accepted his third life. However, he fervently hoped this would be his final "miracle"—he no longer wanted to transmigrate with his memories intact.

Perhaps some people would crave such an incredible miracle, but he did not want it.

It had nothing to do with his two somewhat unsuccessful past lives; he simply felt that a person's life should have a proper beginning and end.

To return to the matter at hand.

The original owner's mother died of "illness" a year ago, the original owner truly died five years ago, and he—the soul-transmigrated arrival—had also nearly been killed by the original owner's childhood friend half a year ago.

Three lives!

In his view, no matter how much emotional debt the original owner's mother owed certain people, it should have been paid off in full by now.

As it happened, half a year ago, this physical body of his had turned twenty years old, fulfilling one of the three requests he had promised the original owner's mother—"You must not leave the Royal Capital before turning twenty; after turning twenty, you may go wherever you please." He had a deep, earnest talk with the King, who was nominally his biological father, and ultimately left the Royal Capital under the pretext of recuperating from an illness.

He thought this had made his stance abundantly clear, and the King had not stopped him.

Yet, certain people's greed knew no bounds, and they had actually pursued him all the way here.

"Raphael! I've finally found you!"

One of the young beastmen in the traveling party shouted excitedly the moment he laid eyes on him.

Handsome Tiger expressionlessly sidestepped two paces to the left.

The newcomer's outstretched arms grabbed only empty air and he even stumbled slightly. Once he regained his footing, he turned to look at Handsome Tiger with an aggrieved expression.

"Raphael Lang Mu, how can you treat me like this? Do you know how hard it was for me all the way here?" the newcomer accused, looking utterly heartbroken.

Handsome Tiger was holding a clay jar and replied with a single word: "Oh."

"Oh? What is that 'oh' supposed to mean? Aren't you happy at all to see me?" the newcomer asked angrily.

With utmost honesty, Handsome Tiger answered: "Not happy."

The newcomer's handsome face crumpled into a ball of wrinkles, and his shoulders slumped: "Raphael, you've changed."

Handsome Tiger: "I've always been like this."

"Raphael, are you still blaming me? That day, I really didn't know—"

"Enough! Ix, scram! It's no use acting like this with Raphael, he doesn't buy your routine." A tall, muscular horned beastman strode over and pushed Ix aside.

"Brother, long time no see." The horned beastman merely extended a fist.

Handsome Tiger also extended his fist and bumped it against the other's.

The few young beastmen behind him also stepped forward one by one to greet Handsome Tiger.

Handsome Tiger nodded at them with a lukewarm expression.

All of them knew Handsome Tiger well; they knew he wasn't unwelcoming toward them, but simply had that kind of personality.

"Let's go talk over there." The horned beastman took the lead and walked aside.

Their group, along with their mounts, had already blocked the main street of the town, drawing the gazes of quite a few onlookers.

Facing the horned beastman, Handsome Tiger's expression softened slightly: "Long time no see, Horned Horse."

Horned Horse gave a dry cough and lowered his voice: "I'll cut straight to the point. Aside from wanting to clear up the misunderstanding between you and Ix, the other reason we came here is that we hope you'll return to the Royal Capital with us."

Handsome Tiger's expression remained unmoved: "Who wants me to go back to the Royal Capital?"

Unable to push away Ix, who was stubbornly trying to eavesdrop, Horned Horse rolled his eyes and said to Handsome Tiger, "Who else could it be besides our boss? Ever since you left, it's been as if he'd lost an arm; his temper has become much more irritable, especially with so many things piling up lately."

chunks.chineseText:
角马左右看看，挨近虎不帅：“王都最近出了一些诡异事件，牵扯到一位大公爵。这事还在调查，后面牵扯颇深。头担心王的安危，这段时间加强了王宫防守力度，同时也在排查王宫里的所有人员。我们几个……因为上次的事，至今还没有恢复原职，正好我们家里也希望我们这段时间离开王都，我们和头商量后，就来这边找你了。”

不等虎不帅表达意见，角马又快速说：“我知道你不想回王都牵扯进那些烂事中。头也知道，他让我告诉你，让你回王都，是因为他缺少帮手，喊你回来是正常，不喊你回来才让人怀疑。但他也同时说，回不回王都全看你自己的意思。”

虎不帅没有给出任何准确回复，岔开话题道：“我带你们先去镇酒馆安顿下来。中午这顿我请。”

“能让你这个吝啬鬼请吃饭，真不容易。”角马开玩笑。

伊克斯在旁边期期艾艾，就想和虎不帅说话。

虎不帅摇摇头，对伊克斯说：“我没怪你。走吧。”

伊克斯脸上的表情顿时跟盛开的太阳花一样，变得灿烂无比：“拉斐尔~，我就知道你不是小心眼的人！你放心，你那天吃的亏，我已经帮你报复回去了。那天晚上，我堵住杜德家那对兄弟把他们打了个半死。后来我见到他们一次打他们一次，打得他们都不敢在王都露头。”

角马没否认，说明伊克斯说的是真的。

但虎不帅一点都不感动。因为他分不清楚伊克斯是真傻还是假傻，是真义气还是伪装义气，他看不透这个人。

伊克斯伸手，想要搂住虎不帅的肩膀。

虎不帅躲开。

伊克斯嘟嘟嚷嚷，无非就是控诉虎不帅就是对好兄弟也不亲近。但他也知道虎不帅一直不喜欢和人太亲密，他也就是习惯性地随口抱怨。

虎不帅把几个曾经是同一个小队的王宫现役但长期休假中的年轻侍卫们带到镇酒馆，把他们安顿下来后，就借口家里还有事，先回去了。

这几个人住在酒馆，他反而不好再继续住在这里。

几个年轻兽人看着虎不帅的背影，其中一人低喃：“拉斐尔对我们明显疏远了。”

角马打圆场：“大家分开有半年，稍微有点疏远也正常，等多处几天就好了。”

“希望能如你所言。”伊克斯面色怅然。

虎不帅回到姨父姨母家里，他的镇长姨父已经听说有外人过来找虎不帅的事。

“我就知道那些人不会放过你。他们果然追来了。”镇长不高兴地说。

“各有各的难处。几个人也各有各的目的，有人是真的想来看看我，有的只是出门避开麻烦，还有的确实带着任务。”虎不帅心里很清楚。

“有人对你打人情牌了吗？”

虎不帅摇头，“真能对我打人情牌的不会现在就出牌。”

“你小心些。”镇长还是不放心。

虎不帅安慰又带着歉意说道：“只要让他们再次确认我已经废掉，而且确实没有影响王的意思，他们会离开的。反倒是您这边，他们可能会想要摸摸镇子的底，以防您和姨母成为我的靠山，进而威胁到其他王子地位。”

镇长冷笑：“那就让他们摸！惹火了我，我直接带着镇子和周边村子加入反叛军。”

虎不帅给了镇长一个“您就别说气话”的眼神。

镇长抬手拍外甥肩膀，没好气地说：“去看你小姨去，别老躲着她走。还有，你要是因为怕给我们带来麻烦就偷偷离开镇子，我就真加入反叛军，不开玩笑。”

虎不帅心里感动。

原身母亲知道他不是她亲儿子，但迪莉娅夫人不知道这点，她和她丈夫一直都把他当至亲的亲人对待和照顾。

其实如果不是他答应原身母亲的请求之一是“在她死后、而他打算离开王都后，必须到迪莉娅身边陪伴她最少一年时间”，他的镇长姨父还在听说他出事后特地跑到王都接他，他也不会在离开王都后来到莫约山谷。

他真的不想把麻烦带给这一家子。

姨父姨母一家对他越好，他越想他们能远离王都混乱。

虎不帅心里想了很多，最后还是顺应镇长的心意，找他小姨请安去了。

哪想到迪莉娅夫人一看到他，就皱眉说：“你被诅咒了。”

同一时间，商非凡也遇到了大-麻烦！
chunks.englishText:
Ma-Jiao looked left and right, then leaned closer to Handsome Tiger: "Some bizarre incidents have occurred in the Royal Capital recently, involving a Grand Duke. The matter is still under investigation, and it runs quite deep behind the scenes. The Boss is worried about the King's safety, so he has stepped up security around the royal palace during this time while also vetting all personnel within it. The few of us... because of the incident last time, still haven't been reinstated to our former positions. Coincidentally, our families also wanted us to leave the Royal Capital for a while, so after discussing it with the Boss, we came all the way here to find you."

Before Handsome Tiger could express his opinion, Ma-Jiao quickly added: "I know you don't want to go back to the Royal Capital and get dragged into that mess. The Boss knows it too, and he told me to let you know: coming back to the Royal Capital is because he lacks helpers, so calling you back is normal—not calling you back is what would make people suspicious. But he also said that whether you return to the Royal Capital or not is entirely up to you."

Handsome Tiger did not give any definite answer. He steered the conversation away: "I'll take you guys to settle down at the town tavern first. Lunch is on me today."

"It's really not easy to get a miser like you to treat us to a meal," Ma-Jiao joked.

Ix lingered nearby, looking eager and hesitant, just wanting to speak with Handsome Tiger.

Handsome Tiger shook his head and said to Ix, "I don't blame you. Let's go."

The expression on Ix's face instantly bloomed like a sunflower, turning radiantly bright: "Raphael~, I knew you weren't a petty person! Don't worry, I've already helped you get revenge for the grievance you suffered that day. That night, I cornered those two brothers from the Dudde family and beat them half to death. After that, I beat them every single time I saw them, until they didn't even dare show their faces in the Royal Capital anymore."

Ma-Jiao didn't refute this, proving that what Ix said was true.

Yet Handsome Tiger felt not a shred of touch or gratitude. Because he couldn't tell whether Ix was genuinely foolish or feigning foolishness, whether he was truly loyal or just putting on an act of loyalty—he simply couldn't see through this person.

Ix reached out, wanting to put an arm around Handsome Tiger's shoulders.

Handsome Tiger dodged out of the way.

Ix muttered complaints, which were nothing more than accusing Handsome Tiger of being distant even with a good brother. But he also knew Handsome Tiger had always disliked being overly intimate with people; he was just casually complaining out of habit.

Handsome Tiger led the several young guards—who were once members of the same royal palace squad and were currently on active status but on extended leave—to the town tavern. After getting them settled, he made the excuse that he still had matters to attend to at home and returned first.

With these fellows staying at the tavern, it would actually be inconvenient for him to continue staying there himself.

The young beastmen watched Handsome Tiger's retreating back, and one of them muttered, "Raphael is clearly distancing himself from us."

Ma-Jiao smoothed things over: "We've been separated for half a year, so a little bit of distance is normal. After spending a few more days together, it'll be fine."

"I hope so," Ix said with a desolate expression.

When Handsome Tiger returned to his aunt and uncle's house, his town-mayor uncle had already heard that outsiders had come looking for him.

"I knew those people wouldn't let you off. They really did chase you down," the mayor said unhappily.

"Everyone has their own difficulties. The few of them also have their own motives; some genuinely wanted to come see me, some just wanted to get away from trouble by stepping out, and others indeed carry orders," Handsome Tiger said, fully aware of the situation.

"Did anyone try playing the emotional card on you?"

Handsome Tiger shook his head. "The ones who are truly qualified to play the emotional card on me won't play it just yet."

"Be careful." The mayor was still uneasy.

Handsome Tiger comforted him while saying apologetically, "As long as I let them confirm once again that my cultivation is crippled and that I truly have no intention of interfering with the King's affairs, they will leave. On the contrary, as for your side, they might want to probe the foundation of this town, just in case you and my aunt become my backers and consequently threaten the status of the other princes."

The mayor sneered, "Then let them probe! If they tick me off, I'll straight-up take the town and the surrounding villages and join the rebels."

Handsome Tiger gave the mayor a look that said, *Please stop spouting angry nonsense.*

The mayor raised a hand and patted his nephew's shoulder, saying with a huff, "Go see your little aunt; stop trying to dodge her all the time. Also, if you secretly run away from the town just because you're afraid of bringing trouble to us, I really will join the rebels, and I'm not joking."

Warmth surged in Handsome Tiger's heart.

The original owner's mother knew he wasn't her biological son, but Madam Delia did not know this; both she and her husband had always treated him and cared for him like a close family member.

In truth, if one of the promises he made to the original owner's mother hadn't been—"after her death, and when you plan to leave the Royal Capital, you must go to Delia's side and accompany her for at least one year"—and if his mayor uncle hadn't traveled all the way to the Royal Capital to pick him up upon hearing he was in trouble, he wouldn't have come to Moyue Valley after leaving the Royal Capital.

He truly did not want to bring trouble to this family.

The better his uncle and aunt's family treated him, the more he wished they could stay far away from the chaos of the Royal Capital.

Handsome Tiger's mind raced with many thoughts, but in the end, he yielded to the mayor's wishes and went to pay his respects to his little aunt.

Never did he expect that the moment Madam Delia laid eyes on him, she would frown and say, "You've been cursed."

At the exact same time, Shang Feifan encountered a big trouble!

chunks.chineseText:
第23章 路遇劫匪

旅程一开始还算顺利，商非凡也切实感受到拥有巨虫坐骑的好处。

狰爷不但跑得快，它还会主动翻越路障、躲避坑陷、跳过地沟，更能提前发现荒野中的野兽给予一定反应。

要么提前躲避，要么直接用速度甩开对方。遇到弱小的，狰爷甚至能直接生吃对方。

字面意思的生吃。

尤其狰爷宽大平坦的背脊十分适合坐卧和站立，只要你能适应它充满想象力的前进方式。

商非凡用绳子在狰爷背脊前方那两根直立的骨刺上编织了一个网兜，把行李和阿呆都塞在那个网兜里，还用绳子拴住，确保狰爷不管怎么折腾也不会把阿呆和行李甩飞出去。

驾驭巨虫坐骑还有一个巨大好处，就是不用考虑路况。

不管是灌木丛、草原、泥坑、乱石带，还是岩石山、蜂窝洞、悬崖，都挡不住狰爷的八只长腿。

就比如刚才他们刚越过一条小河。

看到那条宽度有十来米的小河，商非凡还想着是不是要游过去。

就见狰爷毫不停留地一路跑进河水里，然后扁平的巨大身体就像竹筏一样漂浮在河面上，八只长腿在河水里划拉着，竟然就这么划拉到了对岸。

河水里有阴影划过，看着就像是巨大的鱼类。

但不知道是巨蟹虫坚硬的外壳不适合这些鱼类的牙齿，还是路过的大鱼不想费工夫捕猎，直到爬上对岸，都没有鱼类攻击他们。

狰爷放慢速度等待商非凡给出新的指示。

商非凡也正在判断前行方向。

黑森林城所在方向还是他从铁匠老头嘴里问出来的。

但铁匠老头也不知道前往黑森林城的详细路线，只知道黑森林城是王都的附城，位于天残谷的东南方向。

玩家们没有一个人知道黑森林城在哪里，现在探索游戏地图最远的一拨人就是正在建设玩家二号营地的伏向军他们。

二号营地距离一号营地只有五十公里的直线距离。

不要小看这五十公里，为了拓展出这五十公里，一期玩家和二期玩家每个人都死了不下三次，实际战斗能力比较差的玩家更是死了五六次都有。

玩家们不想往更远处探险吗？

他们当然想，尤其是不愿意按部就班做任务的探险型、自由型玩家。

可是！想在这个世界野外生存真的太难了。

千里走单骑是不存在的，别说千里，千米都不可能。

出门就是找死，敢浪的都翻车。

到最后所有玩家都只能按照游戏开发商给出的地图，先在新手村范围练级。

商非凡如今也深刻认识到他拥有一只巨虫坐骑是有多么幸运。

只看被他抛在身后的那百里路程，如果没有狰爷，他恐怕也只能和其他玩家一样，跟着大部队的推进速度一点点往外扩展，否则就是带着幼崽给荒野虫兽禽鸟鱼送餐的。

“黑森林城在天残谷的东南方向，莫约山谷在黑森林城的北方，也就是说我们得往东走。”

商非凡用脚尖敲击狰爷的背部，给出明确指示：“狰爷，我们向太阳升起的方向走。我早上出门看了黄历，今天利东。”

狰爷没有异意，它还加快了一点速度，就像是前方有什么东西在吸引它。

在一片乱石的荒野地里跑了大约半个小时，商非凡看到了一处天堑。

大地从中间裂开一道巨大的裂缝，裂缝深不可测。

而且这道看不到两头边际的巨大裂缝不但长，还很宽。

商非凡正在想狰爷要怎么跃过这条天堑，就看狰爷已经熟门熟路地顺着裂缝边沿跑起来。

当跑到一处往下的斜坡时，狰爷就溜下了那条斜坡。

“狰爷，我们得越过这条裂缝，去到对面。”商非凡说完模仿振翅声。

狰爷也不知道是理会了老商的意思，还是有它自己的想法，弃耳不闻地一心往裂缝深处跑。

商非凡觉得这只巨蟹虫应该不会自己找死，就站在它的背上，任由它带着他们往深渊里跑。

阿呆抬头看老商，见他老神在在，也不担心了，他还把自己团成一团，窝在网兜里继续睡觉。

就在商非凡以为狰爷要冲进深渊时，就看到狰爷踏上了一道狭窄的石桥。

这条石桥在裂缝往下四十多米的深处，从上面往下看，根本看不到。

裂缝上宽下窄，下面特别黑暗，阳光都照射不进来。

现在商非凡十分确定，狰爷一定来过这里，而且利用这条石桥去往对面也不是第一次。

狰爷驮着一大一小，溜溜地爬过长达三十多米的狭窄石桥，接着身体一横，开始垂直往上爬行。

幸好商非凡已经事先做好准备，连忙用绳子缠紧自己的腰，两只手也紧紧抓住两根骨刺。

行李和阿呆也都已经紧紧绑好、网好，就算狰爷脚朝上翻过来爬行，也不会掉下去。

等爬到裂缝顶端，商非凡重见天日，也看到了裂缝对面的世界。

可还没等他看清楚前方那片黑影是山体，还是人工建造物时，一群也不知道事先埋伏在哪里的兽人突然就杀了出来，把他和巨虫坐骑一起围了起来。

“小子，献上你的坐骑和行李，你和你的幼崽还能活着留在我们这里。”一名脸上戴着骨制面具，胳膊比普通兽人大腿还粗的强壮兽人骑着巨虫，越众而出。

阿呆一个翻身从网兜里坐起来，方方的脑袋探出去，一双眼睛闪闪发亮，哪像一个小呆子。

“打劫？”商非凡像是在笑。

这不是他第一次遇到打劫，应该也不是人生最后一次。

商非凡饶有兴味地看着这群对他和他的行李以及坐骑评头论足的强盗们。

发现这群强盗也许并不太富裕。

首先拥有巨虫坐骑的只有三个强盗。

其次他们的装备和武器都很普通，以皮甲和冷兵器为主。

第三就是他明明只有一个人，带的东西也不多，可这些强盗看到他就两眼放光，一副遇到大肥羊的样子。

想来这条路上能让他们打劫的行商和行人并不多，以至于遇到一个都如此兴奋。

这些兽人不会就是那位天残谷主口中的强盗窝中的强盗吧？

如果是，那还真的很巧。

早知就在谷主那里领一个打探强盗窝的侦查任务。

不过想想也没什么可惜的，如果奖励只能到玩家营地的杂货铺领取，他如果不掉头回去，那不管有多少奖励，他短时间内都领不到。

戴面具的强壮兽人：“不，是过路费。不过你非要认为是打劫也可以。”

“爸爸，干他们！”阿呆突然很大声地喊道。

商非凡惊讶低头：没想到你小子竟然是这样的。

一群强盗兽人发出哄笑。

“我是一名到处跑的修理商，也许我可以帮你们一点小忙，比如修理你们的工具和武器。免费帮你们修三样物品，你们只要出原材料，然后让我们过去如何？”商非凡看向强壮兽人，好声好气地商量。

同时，商非凡的脚尖在狰爷背部点击出特殊节奏——兄弟，听我指令，一起冲出包围圈啊。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 23: Encountering Bandits on the Road (Part 1)

The journey began quite smoothly, and Shang Feifan truly experienced the benefits of owning a giant insect mount.

Not only could Lord Zhen run fast, but it would also actively climb over roadblocks, dodge pits and trenches, and leap across ditches. It could even spot wild beasts in the wilderness ahead of time and react accordingly.

Either it would dodge in advance, or it would simply shake them off with sheer speed. When encountering weak ones, Lord Zhen could even swallow them alive on the spot.

Swallowed alive, literally.

In particular, Lord Zhen's wide and flat back was extremely suitable for sitting, lying, and standing—provided you could get used to its imaginative way of moving forward.

Shang Feifan used a rope to weave a net pouch between the two upright bone spikes at the front of Lord Zhen's back, stuffing both his luggage and Ah-Dai inside that net pouch, and securing it tightly with ropes to ensure that no matter how much Lord Zhen tossed about, it wouldn't fling Ah-Dai and the luggage away.

Another huge advantage of riding a giant insect mount was that one didn't need to consider road conditions at all.

Whether it was brushwood, grasslands, mud pits, boulder fields, rocky mountains, honeycomb caves, or cliffs, none of them could stop Lord Zhen's eight long legs.

Take, for example, just a moment ago when they had crossed a small river.

Seeing that river, which was about ten meters wide, Shang Feifan had been wondering if they needed to swim across.

Then he saw Lord Zhen march unhesitatingly right into the river water, whereupon its flat, gigantic body floated on the river surface like a bamboo raft, its eight long legs paddling through the water until it actually paddled all the way to the opposite bank.

Shadows glided past within the river water, looking somewhat like gigantic fish.

However, whether it was because the giant crab-bug's hard exoskeleton was unsuited for the teeth of these fish, or because the large fish passing by didn't want to waste effort hunting, no fish attacked them until they crawled ashore on the opposite bank.

Lord Zhen slowed its pace, waiting for Shang Feifan to give new instructions.

Shang Feifan was also assessing their direction of travel.

The direction toward Black Forest City was something he had pried out of the old blacksmith's mouth.

However, the old blacksmith didn't know the detailed route to Black Forest City either; he only knew that Black Forest City was a satellite city of the Royal Capital, located to the southeast of the Heavenly Maimed Valley.

Not a single player knew where Black Forest City was. The furthest group currently exploring the game map was Fu Xiangjun and his crew, who were in the midst of constructing Player Camp No. 2.

Camp No. 2 was only a straight-line distance of fifty kilometers away from Camp No. 1.

Do not underestimate these fifty kilometers; in order to expand this fifty-kilometer radius, players from the first and second waves had each died no less than three times, while players with relatively poor combat capabilities had died five or six times.

Did players not want to explore further out?

Of course they wanted to, especially exploration-type and freedom-type players who were unwilling to do quests step-by-step.

However! Surviving in the wilderness of this world was simply too difficult.

Traveling alone for a thousand miles did not exist; forget a thousand miles, even a single thousand meters was impossible.

Stepping out the door was courting death, and anyone who dared to act wildly inevitably crashed and burned.

In the end, all players could only follow the map provided by the game developers and grind levels within the vicinity of the novice village.

Shang Feifan now deeply realized how fortunate he was to possess a giant insect mount.

Just looking at the hundred-li stretch of distance he had left behind—if not for Lord Zhen, he probably would have had to crawl outward step by step along with the main force's advancing speed just like the other players, otherwise he would have ended up delivering takeout to the wilderness insects, beasts, birds, and fish along with his cub.

"Black Forest City is to the southeast of Heavenly Maimed Valley, and Moyue Valley is to the north of Black Forest City. In other words, we need to head east."

Shang Feifan tapped the tips of his toes against Lord Zhen's back, giving clear instructions: "Lord Zhen, let's walk in the direction where the sun rises. I checked the almanac when I went out this morning; today is auspicious for heading east."

Lord Zhen had no objections; it even accelerated slightly, as if something ahead was attracting it.

Running through a boulder-strewn wilderness for about half an hour, Shang Feifan spotted a natural chasm.

The earth had split open down the middle into a gigantic fissure, bottomless and unfathomable.

Moreover, this massive fissure, whose edges could not be seen from either end, was not only long, but also very wide.

Just as Shang Feifan was wondering how Lord Zhen was going to leap across this chasm, he saw that Lord Zhen was already running with practiced familiarity along the edge of the fissure.

When it reached a downward slope, Lord Zhen slid right down it.

"Lord Zhen, we need to cross this fissure and get to the other side." Shang Feifan finished speaking and imitated the sound of flapping wings.

Whether Lord Zhen understood Old Shang's meaning or had ideas of its own, it turned a deaf ear and single-mindedly ran deeper into the fissure.

Shang Feifan figured this giant crab-bug shouldn't be courting death on its own, so he stood on its back, letting it carry them down into the abyss.

Ah-Dai looked up at Old Shang, and seeing him completely calm and collected, he stopped worrying as well. He curled himself up into a ball, nestled back into the net pouch, and went back to sleep.

Just when Shang Feifan thought Lord Zhen was going to charge headfirst into the abyss, he saw the giant bug step onto a narrow stone bridge.

This stone bridge was located over forty meters down the depths of the fissure; looking down from above, it was completely invisible.

The fissure was wide at the top and narrow at the bottom, and the lower sections were pitch-black, completely shutting out the sunlight.

By now, Shang Feifan was entirely certain that Lord Zhen had definitely been here before, and this wasn't its first time using this stone bridge to cross to the other side.

Carrying one adult and one child, Lord Zhen scuttled smoothly across the narrow stone bridge, which was over thirty meters long. Then, its body turned sideways, and it began climbing vertically upward.

Fortunately, Shang Feifan had made preparations in advance, hurriedly wrapping a rope tightly around his waist and gripping two bone spikes firmly with both hands.

His luggage and Ah-Dai were also tightly bound and netted; even if Lord Zhen flipped upside down with its feet facing the sky to climb, they wouldn't fall off.

When they climbed to the top of the fissure, Shang Feifan saw the light of day once more, and also laid eyes on the world on the opposite side of the fissure.

However, before he could clearly see whether the dark shadows ahead were mountain ranges or artificial structures, a group of beastmen—who knew where they had been lying in ambush—suddenly burst out and surrounded him and his giant insect mount.

"Kid, hand over your mount and your luggage, and you and your cub can be allowed to stay here alive." A heavily built beastman wearing a bone mask on his face and arms thicker than an ordinary beastman's thighs rode a giant bug, stepping out from the crowd.

Ah-Dai flipped over and sat up from the net pouch, sticking out his square-shaped head. His pair of eyes flashed brightly, looking nothing like a little dummy.

"A robbery?" Shang Feifan asked, smiling.

This wasn't his first time encountering a robbery, nor would it likely be the last in his life.

Shang Feifan looked with keen interest at this group of bandits who were evaluating him, his luggage, and his mount.

He discovered that this band of robbers might not be very wealthy.

First of all, only three of the bandits possessed giant insect mounts.

Secondly, their equipment and weapons were very ordinary, primarily consisting of leather armor and cold steel weaponry.

Thirdly, even though he was all by himself and carrying very few things, these bandits' eyes lit up the moment they saw him, wearing the expression of someone who had struck a fat sheep.

Presumably, the number of merchants and travelers passing by this route whom they could rob was so scarce that encountering even one made them this excited.

Could these beastmen be the bandits belonging to the bandit den mentioned by the Lord of Heavenly Maimed Valley?

If so, that would be quite a coincidence.

If he had known, he should have accepted a scouting quest to investigate the bandit den from the Valley Lord.

Still, thinking about it, there was nothing to regret; if the rewards could only be claimed at the grocery store in the player camp, then unless he turned back, he wouldn't be able to claim any rewards in the short term, no matter how many there were.

The masked, muscular beastman said: "No, it's a toll fee. But if you insist on calling it a robbery, that's fine too."

"Dad, trash them!" Ah-Dai suddenly shouted out loud.

Shang Feifan lowered his head in surprise: *I didn't expect you to be this kind of kid.*

The group of bandit beastmen burst into roaring laughter.

"I'm a traveling repairman. Perhaps I can do you a small favor, such as repairing your tools and weapons. I'll repair three items for free; you just need to provide the raw materials, and then let us pass. How about that?" Shang Feifan looked at the muscular beastman and negotiated in a pleasant tone.

At the same time, the toe of Shang Feifan's shoe tapped out a special rhythm on Lord Zhen's back—*Bro, listen to my command, let's charge out of the encirclement together.*

chunks.chineseText:
随后又对阿呆低声叮嘱：“待在网兜里，不管发生什么，不要出来。”

阿呆迅速缩回网兜里。

强壮兽人冷笑一声，抬起胳膊，用力一挥：“抓住他们，要活的！”

一群强盗发出怪叫，一颗黑色圆溜溜的东西突然扔向狰爷。

就是现在！商非凡对狰爷给出冲击信号，抓住工兵铲，腿部跟装了弹簧一样，高高跳起，主动冲向那颗不明物体。

啪！

铲面拍中那不明物体。

不明物体炸开，一股灰黄色烟雾弥漫而起。

狰爷突然掉头，以极快的速度冲向后方地裂。

“拦住它！别让那巨蟹虫跑了！”

几个强盗飞速绷直一条长绳。

可狰爷竟然来了个极速刹车，然后跳起来，一头冲进地裂中。

拍中不明物体的商非凡从半空落下。

他的巨虫坐骑呢？！

他明明和狰爷商量好的，他们要打配合，他都算好了，他落下时，会正好落在冲刺的狰爷背上，然后狰爷会带着他往前冲，冲出包围圈。

可现在他那么大一只坐骑呢？

为什么狰爷不像他们约定一样地往前面跑，还反过来跳进了后面的地裂里？

商非凡一个落地翻滚，爬起，抬头：因为这个发出强烈难闻气味的灰黄色烟雾吗？

更糟糕的是，在闻到这股难闻气味后，商非凡头晕了，眼睛看到的景象也出现了重影。

“巨虫和幼崽都跑了，还有那游商带的行李！操-他虫祖，这次亏大了！”

“抓住那个游商！他不是说他是修理商吗，以后就留他在我们寨子里做活！”

“就怕他不会老实听话。”

“不听话就打断他的腿，修理工只要有手就能做活。再不听话就卖了他！”

麻烦大了。

商非凡想要查看自己的状态，却想起来他还没有开通相关功能。

商非凡后悔了，早知他就不嫌弃那些各有缺点的特殊物品，先装备一个再说。

商非凡思绪很快，动作也很快，当即屏住呼吸，趁着还有力气，抓起工兵铲就朝人最少的方向冲过去。

“拦住他！”

“艹！他怎么还有劲冲得这么快！”

“小心！”

一名强盗兽人被挑飞了起来，半边肩膀被划拉出一个巨大口子，鲜血哗啦啦往外冒。

商非凡挑翻一个，又拍向第二个拦住他去路的兽人。

兽人不信邪地与商非凡对抗，却被拍得吱哇惨叫。

“他力气好大！”

“别让他冲出包围圈！多来点人！”

“绳子拦不住他！他力气太大了！用网！用铁藤网拦住他！”

“这家伙太难缠了！为什么他到现在还没昏过去？”

商非凡想要躲过那张巨大又粗实的网，但他眼前景象越来越模糊，力气也快速从身体里流失，他的意识已经没办法顺利操纵他的双腿。

最后，商非凡只记得自己横过工兵铲，用锋利的刀刃去切割铁藤网，顺便还划伤了几个想要靠近他的兽人强盗。

但他的速度越来越慢，终于，他被那张铁藤网给死死缠住了。

“拉紧！绊倒他！”

商非凡四肢被缠住，当他被绊倒在地时，他也彻底失去了意识。
chunks.englishText:
Then he gave A-Dai a low, stern warning: "Stay inside the mesh bag. No matter what happens, do not come out."

A-Dai quickly shrank back into the mesh bag.

The brawny Orc sneered, raised his arm, and swung it down forcefully: "Catch them! I want them alive!"

A group of bandits let out bizarre, shrieking yells, and a dark, round object was suddenly hurled toward the Zhen-beast.

*Now is the time!* Shang Feifan gave the Zhen-beast the signal to charge, grabbed his military entrenching tool, and leaped high into the air with his legs acting like coiled springs, launching himself straight toward the unidentified projectile.

*Clap!*

The blade of the shovel slapped solidly against the strange object.

The object exploded, and a billowing cloud of grayish-yellow smoke instantly spread through the air.

The Zhen-beast abruptly spun around and bolted backward at breakneck speed toward the fissure in the ground.

"Stop it! Don't let that giant beetle-crab get away!"

Several bandits rapidly pulled a long rope taut across its path.

Yet, the Zhen-beast executed an astonishing, high-speed screeching halt, leaped forward, and plunged headfirst straight into the earth fissure.

Shang Feifan fell back down from mid-air.

*What about his giant insect mount?!*

He had explicitly coordinated with the Zhen-beast; they were supposed to work as a team! He had calculated everything—when he dropped down, he would land right on the back of the charging Zhen-beast, and the beast would carry him forward, breaking straight out of the encirclement.

So where in the world was his massive mount now?

Why didn't the Zhen-beast run forward as they had agreed, but instead turned around and jumped backward into the fissure?

Shang Feifan executed a rolling landing, scrambled to his feet, and looked up: *Was it because of this grayish-yellow smoke with its intensely foul odor?*

Worse still, upon inhaling the noxious smell, Shang Feifan felt his head spin, and his vision doubled.

"Both the giant bug and the cub got away, not to mention the caravan's cargo! Son of a bug-ancestor, we took a huge loss this time!"

"Grab that traveling merchant! Didn't he say he was a repairman? We'll keep him in the stronghold to do hard labor from now on!"

"I'm worried he won't obey us honestly."

"If he doesn't obey, break his legs. A mechanic only needs his hands to work. If he's still disobedient, sell him off!"

*We've got a big problem.*

Shang Feifan wanted to check his status interface, only to remember he hadn't unlocked the relevant features yet.

Shang Feifan instantly regretted it. Had he known, he wouldn't have disdained those flawed special items; he should have equipped at least one beforehand.

His thoughts raced, and his actions were equally swift. Holding his breath while he still had some strength left, Shang Feifan grabbed his entrenching tool and charged toward the direction with the fewest enemies.

"Stop him!"

"Damn it! How does he still have the energy to charge this fast?!"

"Watch out!"

An Orc bandit was scooped up into the air, a massive gash ripped across half his shoulder as fresh blood gushed outward in torrents.

Shang Feifan flipped one bandit over with his shovel and swung it toward a second Orc blocking his path.

The Orc stubbornly tried to counterattack, only to be smacked away with piercing shrieks of pain.

"He's ridiculously strong!"

"Don't let him break through the encirclement! Bring more men!"

"The rope can't hold him! His strength is too great! Use the net! Use the iron-vine net to stop him!"

"This bastard is too stubborn! Why hasn't he passed out yet?!"

Shang Feifan tried to duck under the massive, thick net, but the scenery before his eyes grew increasingly blurry, and his strength rapidly drained from his body. His consciousness could no longer properly control his legs.

In the end, all Shang Feifan could remember was holding his entrenching tool horizontally, using its sharp edge to hack at the iron-vine net, incidentally slashing a few Orc bandits who tried to get close.

However, his movements grew slower and slower until, finally, he was tightly and inextricably bound by the iron-vine net.

"Pull tight! Trip him!"

With all four limbs entangled, Shang Feifan crashed heavily to the ground, and at that moment, he completely lost consciousness.

chunks.chineseText:
第24章 鬼鬼祟祟的玻璃球

游戏世界果然不讲科学！

他看得很清楚，那黑色圆形物体绝不是人工制造物，那就是一枚果实。他已经足够提防，才想要在那枚果实落下前把它拍飞。

可那枚果实的外皮竟然那么脆弱，刚碰上就炸开了。

它不但炸开，还爆发出那么多烟雾！

就那么一枚果实，在那么空旷的野外，还有风的情况下，竟然能把烟雾扩散到那么大面积还能保持浓度！

现实世界的烟雾-弹想要在空旷野外达到这种效果，至少需要十几枚。

更别说这种果实炸-弹还能致使人昏迷。

他现在终于明白那些强盗兽人为什么都戴着难看的骨质面具，显然那些面具和防毒面罩一个功效。

很好，他以后会牢牢记住，这就是一个不科学的世界！

不，也许应该说，这是一个科学和魔幻并存的世界。

不过商非凡也承认，如果这里是现实世界，他肯定会处理得更谨慎一点，而不是那么莽地直接跳起来拍飞“炸-弹”。

就因为他抱着游戏心态，现在他就只能蹲在地牢里玩铁窗泪。

他的手腕和脚腕还分别戴上了手铐和脚镣，脚镣还特别短特别重，导致他走路都只能走小碎步。

地牢不大，最多只有六平，没有窗户，又黑又臭又潮湿，尿骚味特别重。

虫子很多，爬来爬去。

更糟糕的是，那些该死的强盗把他身上的衣服鞋袜全都脱了，连头发都剃了个精光。

哦，顺便说一句，他的尾巴回来了。

希望那些强盗没有亲眼看到他尾巴长出来的过程。

商非凡靠着墙壁站立，他脸上不见半点怒火，也不见羞愤。

强盗对他做的不过是常规手段。

战区对手抓到俘虏，那是从里到外都要检查一遍，包括皮肤下面，就为了防止被捕者在身上藏有某些小零件。

这种“扒皮”手段也能有效打击被俘者的自尊，羞辱他们，击垮被俘者的心理防线。

为此，更过分的事也有。

商非凡现在就暗暗庆幸那些强盗没有极端到连他的牙齿都拔掉。

现实世界他会在自己身上各处藏东西，但这是游戏！

好吧，他在头发里藏了一根铁丝，但现在他的头发都被剃光，那根铁丝肯定也被发现。

同样，他藏在衣服鞋袜里的一些小东西就算不被发现，也拿不回来了。

商非凡还真没想过要在游戏身体的牙齿里藏东西，下次他会记得备上。

等等，这里是游戏世界，把地牢做成这样，还给玩家这样的“遭遇”，就不怕无法过审？

还是说这个游戏受众不是面向全世界，也不是全年龄向？

可就算有年龄分界线，女玩家也无法接受这种遭遇吧？

商非凡在心中留下一个疑惑。

他暂时把注意力放在了脱困上。

但那些强盗似乎特别有经验，这间狭窄黑暗的地牢里连根干草都没有。作为栅栏的牢门也特别结实，缝隙狭窄到只能伸出两根手指，栏杆都有儿臂粗。

找不到适合开锁的物品，商非凡就试着能不能用力气挣断锁链。

但他发现自己竟然用不上力气，似乎那枚果实炸-弹的毒性还没有完全从他身体里代谢掉。

看来，他只有暂等机会。

或者干脆下线去找伏向军，看能不能召集一批玩家来把自己救出去。

再不行，他也可以玩自杀，直接死回出生点。

总之，他并不担心自己，只稍微担心被狰爷带跑的阿呆。

好在阿呆并不是真呆，他的行李也都在狰爷背上，里面光是干粮清水就足够阿呆吃十天半个月。

如果狰爷聪明，很可能会返回族地。

而狰爷只要返回族地，就代表回到了天残村。那么阿呆也会相对安全。

当然这都是往好的发展想，阿呆和狰爷也有可能遇到不好的事情，但他现在被困在这里，就算再担心也没用。

商非凡把思绪重新转回到如何脱困上。

自杀可以先放一边，他想那些强盗抓住他后没有立即杀死他，肯定有想利用他的地方。

不管是希望他留在强盗窝当修理工，还是把他当奴隶卖掉，那都会是他的机会。

他现在只要耐心等待。

那些强盗应该不会那么快把他放出去。

商非凡很懂这些人的手法，他自己就很擅长此道。

比如先把人关在黑暗狭窄的空间里，关上一段时间，连食水都不提供，名为熬鹰。

所以……商非凡坐到墙角打开了脑载系统的游戏商城。

之前他都没有仔细看过游戏商城里的商品，现在他可以定下心来仔细看看了。

同时他发现在他昏迷期间，他的任务栏多了一个任务。

【任务十七，设法逃出地牢，成功后奖励1贡献点。】

目前他赚到的贡献点一共有6点，他就把6个贡献点能买到的商品全都罗列出来，再从中寻找对自己现状有帮助的物品。

排除天赋技能和职业技能这两类，原因还是价格太贵，他买不起。

特殊物品中有一把万能-钥匙，非神秘侧物品，只需要5个贡献点，能开所有物理系的锁。

如果商非凡现在手头有很多贡献点，他一定会毫不犹豫地买下这把万能-钥匙，但他现在不得不多想一想。

一次死亡，一次被抓，很大原因都是因为他无法监控自己身体的实际状况。

如果他能在身体出现明显状况前，就知道自己中了什么buff，并能知道buff的效果和持续时间，那对他做出有效对应会有极大帮助。

如果是现实世界，他自然不会期求有这么魔幻的监测效果，但现实世界也没这么多让他防不胜防的花招。

而且他想逃出地牢，也得弄清楚致使他身体无力的毒性还要持续多久，以及是否需要特别解毒。

所以能监测身体状况的商品，这次无论如何都得买一个装备上。

扣除他想购买的buff监测商品，他能动用的贡献点只剩下2点。

他还想买一个可以防毒抗毒的商品，如果能让他百毒不侵最好。

有这样效果的商品不少，特殊物品中就有一个抵抗自然类毒雾的防毒面具，只要3个贡献点。

食品中有一种祛毒果，吃掉后三天内可以预防绝大多数毒素，中毒后服下也能拖延毒发时间，需要6个贡献点。

药物中也有能解毒祛毒的，但在不知道他中的毒素属于哪种毒素前，他也不能随便买解毒-药物。

最后，商非凡的目光落到生活用品和材料上，对比价格后，目前对他最有用也最划算的是一把多功能链锯，只要3个贡献点就能买到。

商非凡按照需求程度的轻重缓急做了个排列。

搞清楚身上的毒素并解决它，才是最重要的。

否则逃出去却无力抗敌，也没力气跑路，到时候还是会被抓回来。

还会打草惊蛇，让强盗们对他的看管更严，打断他的腿也不是不可能。

商非凡一旦下定决心，就不会再犹豫。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 24: The Sneaky Glass Orb (Part 1)

The game world truly defied all science!

He had seen it clearly: that round black object was definitely not man-made; it was a fruit. He had been cautious enough to try and swat it away before it could land.

Yet the skin of that fruit was incredibly fragile, exploding the moment it made contact.

Not only did it explode, but it also released an immense amount of smoke!

Just a single fruit, in such an open wilderness and with the wind blowing, could spread smoke over such a vast area while maintaining its density!

In the real world, achieving this kind of effect with smoke grenades in an open field would require at least a dozen of them.

Not to mention, this fruit bomb could actually induce unconsciousness.

Now he finally understood why those bandit beastmen wore those ugly bone masks. Clearly, those masks served the same purpose as gas masks.

Very well. He would firmly keep in mind that this was an unscientific world!

No, perhaps it would be more accurate to say that this was a world where science and magic coexisted.

However, Shang Feifan also admitted that if this were the real world, he would have handled it much more cautiously instead of recklessly leaping up to swat away a "bomb."

Precisely because he had maintained a gamer's mindset, he was now stuck in a dungeon, staring at iron bars.

His wrists and ankles were bound with handcuffs and shackles. The shackles were exceptionally short and heavy, forcing him to take tiny, shuffling steps.

The dungeon was small, barely six square meters at most. It had no windows, and was dark, smelly, and damp, reeking heavily of urine.

Bugs were everywhere, crawling all over the place.

To make matters worse, those damned bandits had stripped him of all his clothes, shoes, and socks, and had even shaved his head completely bald.

Oh, and by the way, his tail was back.

He hoped those bandits hadn't witnessed the process of his tail growing back with their own eyes.

Shang Feifan stood leaning against the wall. There was no trace of anger or humiliation on his face.

What the bandits had done to him was merely standard procedure.

In a war zone, when enemies captured a prisoner, they would search them thoroughly from inside out, even under the skin, to prevent the captive from hiding small components on their body.

This "skinning" method was also highly effective at crushing a captive's self-esteem, humiliating them, and breaking their psychological defenses.

For this purpose, even more extreme measures were common.

Shang Feifan was secretly glad that these bandits weren't extreme enough to pull out his teeth.

In the real world, he would hide things all over his body, but this was a game!

Well, he had hidden a piece of wire in his hair, but now that his head was shaved, that wire had undoubtedly been discovered.

Similarly, even if the small items he hid in his clothes, shoes, and socks hadn't been found, he couldn't get them back now anyway.

Shang Feifan had never actually thought about hiding things in his game character's teeth. He would remember to prepare that next time.

Wait, this was a game world. Making the dungeon like this and subjecting players to such an "experience"—weren't they afraid of failing censorship reviews?

Or was this game not targeted at a global audience, nor was it for all ages?

But even with an age rating, female players wouldn't be able to accept this kind of treatment, right?

Shang Feifan left the question lingering in his mind.

For now, he focused his attention on escaping.

But those bandits seemed exceptionally experienced. There wasn't even a single blade of straw in this narrow, dark dungeon. The barred cell door was also incredibly sturdy; the gaps were so narrow that he could only stick two fingers through, and the bars were as thick as a child's arm.

Unable to find anything suitable for lockpicking, Shang Feifan tried to see if he could use brute strength to snap the chains.

But he found that he couldn't exert any strength. It seemed the toxin from that fruit bomb had not yet been fully metabolized by his body.

It appeared he could only bide his time.

Or he could simply log off and find Fu Xiangjun to see if they could gather a group of players to rescue him.

If all else failed, he could commit suicide and respawn back at the starting point.

In short, he wasn't worried about himself; he was only slightly worried about Ah Dai, who had been carried off by Zhengye.

Fortunately, Ah Dai wasn't truly simple-minded, and his luggage was on Zhengye's back. The dry rations and fresh water alone would last Ah Dai for ten to fifteen days.

If Zhengye was smart, he would likely return to the clan territory.

And as long as Zhengye returned to the clan territory, it meant returning to Tiancan Village. Ah Dai would be relatively safe there.

Of course, these were optimistic scenarios. Ah Dai and Zhengye could also run into trouble, but since he was trapped here, worrying would do no good.

Shang Feifan turned his thoughts back to how to escape.

Suicide could be put aside for now. He figured that since the bandits hadn't killed him immediately after capturing him, they must have some use for him.

Whether they wanted him to stay in the bandit camp as a repairman or sell him off as a slave, it would present an opportunity.

All he had to do now was wait patiently.

The bandits probably wouldn't let him out anytime soon.

Shang Feifan understood these people's methods very well; he was an expert at this himself.

For instance, locking someone in a dark, cramped space for a period of time without food or water—a technique known as "taming the falcon."

So... Shang Feifan sat in the corner of the wall and opened the game mall in his brain-hosted system.

He hadn't looked closely at the items in the game mall before, but now he could settle his mind and examine them thoroughly.

At the same time, he discovered that a new quest had been added to his quest log during his unconsciousness.

[Quest 17: Find a way to escape the dungeon. Reward upon success: 1 Contribution Point.]

Currently, he had earned a total of 6 Contribution Points. He listed all the items that could be purchased with 6 Contribution Points and searched for anything that could help his current situation.

He excluded talent skills and class skills, simply because they were too expensive for him to afford.

Among the special items, there was a Skeleton Key. It was a non-mystical item that cost only 5 Contribution Points and could open any physical lock.

If Shang Feifan had plenty of Contribution Points on hand, he would have bought this Skeleton Key without hesitation. But now, he had to think things through.

His one death and one capture were largely because he couldn't monitor his body's actual condition.

If he could know what buffs or debuffs he had before his body showed obvious symptoms, along with their effects and durations, it would be of immense help in making effective responses.

In the real world, he naturally wouldn't expect such a magical monitoring effect, but the real world didn't have so many unpredictable tricks that caught him off guard either.

Furthermore, if he wanted to escape the dungeon, he had to figure out how long the weakness-inducing toxin would last and whether he needed a specific antidote.

Therefore, no matter what, he had to buy and equip an item that could monitor his physical condition this time.

Deducting the buff-monitoring item he wanted to buy, he would only have 2 Contribution Points left to spend.

He also wanted to buy an item that provided poison resistance or immunity—ideally, something that made him completely immune to all poisons.

There were quite a few items with such effects. Among the special items, there was a gas mask that resisted natural toxic mists, costing only 3 Contribution Points.

Among the food items, there was a Detoxification Fruit. Eating it would prevent most toxins for three days, and consuming it after being poisoned could delay the onset of the poison. It cost 6 Contribution Points.

There were also medicines that could detoxify, but without knowing what kind of toxin he had been poisoned with, he couldn't just buy any random antidote.

Finally, Shang Feifan's gaze fell upon daily necessities and materials. After comparing the prices, the most useful and cost-effective item for him at the moment was a multi-functional chainsaw, which could be bought for just 3 Contribution Points.

Shang Feifan prioritized his needs in order of urgency.

Figuring out the toxin in his body and resolving it was the most important thing.

Otherwise, even if he escaped, he wouldn't have the strength to fight enemies or run away, and he would just be captured again.

It would also alert the enemy, causing the bandits to guard him even more strictly, and breaking his legs was not out of the question.

Once Shang Feifan made up his mind, he would no longer hesitate.

<<<CHAPTER_START id="chunk-1789493738055-48-klrtx" index=49 title="第24章 鬼鬼祟祟的玻璃球 (Part 2)">>>
He spent 4 Contribution Points to purchase the special item: [Cracked Glass Orb].

This thing was considered the most dangerous of the four items capable of monitoring physical conditions. Its primary function seemed to be assisting with curses, while its secondary function was monitoring curses cast upon oneself by others. Its biggest drawback was that equipping it carried the risk of being dragged into the dark world.

However, this item could also monitor non-curse buffs and debuffs, and it could even conceal one's own physical condition.

In terms of versatility and practicality, Shang Feifan was willing to bear the risk of being dragged into the dark world.

Besides, it was just a game. Why overthink it?

Maybe the dark world would be even more fun.

Once the item was in his possession, before Shang Feifan could even open his palm to take a proper look at this special purchase...

...the cracked glass orb flew straight out of his palm and plunged directly into his right eye.

Shang Feifan let out a muffled groan of pain, clutching his right eye.

Damn this 100% pain sensitivity!

It hurt like absolute hell!

Who could have guessed this crappy glass orb would burrow into his eye?!

...

Shang Feifan didn't know how long he lay there. Before he could even think of logging off, he blacked out.

Interestingly, falling unconscious in the game didn't automatically log him out.

The thought merely flashed through Shang Feifan's mind, and he didn't pay much attention to it, assuming it was the same for all other players.

When he opened his eyes again, he found that his field of vision had undergone a new change.

He seemed to see distorted lines of light and flickering symbols.

But before he could get a clear look, a sharp pain stabbed through his brain.

Subsequently, several lines of bizarre symbols popped up in the vision of his right eye.

These strange symbols shifted and twisted, eventually resolving into neat text in the Common Tongue of the Beastman World.

[Warning! Mental Strength damaged. Cause of damage: Forcible observation of the world's primal energy composition. Mental Strength: 16 (-14)/100. Recommendation: Immediately consume medicine or food that restores and soothes mental strength. Deep meditation is recommended immediately to recover mental strength. Natural recovery to full value requires 72 hours.]

[Warning! Body poisoned. Source of toxin: Stink-Mist Fruit. The mist of this fruit causes biological bodies to become limp and weak. Strength: 19 (-15)/100, Agility: 11 (-8)/100, Health Points: 99 (-29)/100. Estimated toxin excretion time is approximately 24 hours; 17 hours remaining. No special treatment required, no residual toxins will remain. To detoxify early, targeted medicine or food may be consumed.]

Both warnings were perfectly normal, making Shang Feifan feel that this cracked glass orb was well worth the purchase.

Worth it enough that he could overlook the extreme agony of the glass orb burrowing into his eye moments ago.

But in addition to these two warnings, he saw two more notifications.

The text of these two notifications was tiny, carrying an inexplicably eerie and sneaky vibe.

[Family, are you currently filled with rage, wishing to curse the bastards who captured and harmed you? Come, let us loudly curse those who have wronged you. All you need to do before cursing is chant three times: "O supreme and great existence, God of Curses, Konizeus, I shall offer a sacrifice. Please help me curse my enemies."]

[Almost forgot to mention: the sacrifice will determine the effect and range of the curse.]

Shang Feifan: "..."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第24章 鬼鬼祟祟的玻璃球 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
他花了4点贡献点，购买了特殊物品【破碎的玻璃球】。

这玩意在四个能监测身体状况的物品中算是最危险的一个，它的主要功能似乎是辅助诅咒，附加功能才是监测他人对自己的诅咒情况，最大缺点就是装备这玩意有可能被拉入黑暗世界。

但这玩意还能同时监测非诅咒类的buff，还可以遮掩自身的身体状况。

从功能的多样性和实用性来说，商非凡愿意承担被拉入黑暗世界的危险。

再说游戏嘛，想那么多干什么。

说不定黑暗世界更好玩呢。

东西到手，商非凡还没有摊开手掌好好看一看他购买的这个特殊商品。

那个破碎的玻璃球竟然直接从他的手掌里飞出来，一头撞入他的右眼中。

商非凡疼得闷哼一声，捂住了右眼。

该死的百分百痛觉！

太他妈疼了！

谁能想到这个破玻璃球会往他眼睛里钻？！

……

商非凡不知道自己躺了多久，他甚至都没有来得及想到下线，人就昏迷了。

有意思的是，他在游戏中昏迷竟然不会自动下线。

商非凡脑中只快速飘过这个想法，也没有多留意，他以为其他玩家都是如此。

当他再睁开眼睛，他发现他的视界有了新的变化。

他似乎看到了一些扭曲的光线和跳动的符号。

但还没等他看清，他的脑子就一阵刺痛。

随后，他的右眼视界中就跳出几行诡异的符号。

这些诡异符号变来变去扭来扭去，最终变成了整齐的兽人世界通用语。

【警告！精神力受损，受损原因为强行观看世界能量本源构成，精神力值16(-14)/100。建议立刻服用修复缓和精神力的药物或食物，建议立刻进行深度冥想恢复精神力。自然恢复到满值需要72小时。】

【警告！身体中毒，毒源为臭雾果，该果实雾气可致使生物身体酥软无力。力量19（-15）/100，敏捷11（-8）/100，生命值99（-29）/100。预计毒素排出时间约为24小时，现剩余17小时。无需特殊治疗，不会有残留余毒，想要提前解毒，可服用针对性药物或食物。】

这两段提醒都非常正常，也让商非凡觉得这个破碎的玻璃球买的很值。

值到他可以忽略刚才玻璃球钻眼给他带来的极致痛楚。

但除了这两段提醒，他还看到了两段提醒。

这两段提醒的文字很小，莫名有种鬼唧唧的鬼鬼祟祟感。

【家人，你现在是否满心愤怒，想要诅咒抓捕和伤害你的混蛋？来吧，让我们大声诅咒那些对不起你的人，而你只要在诅咒之前念三遍‘至高伟大的存在，诅咒之神科尼泽厄斯，我将奉上祭品，请帮我诅咒我的敌人’。】

【差点忘了说，祭品将决定诅咒的效果和范围。】

商非凡：“……”
