而且有一说一，这吸怨气真的让他比洗桑拿还舒服。

大概是他这个空气净化器太得力，没一会儿，这小木屋的光线都看起来亮堂许多。

虎不帅眼中闪过一丝诧异。

他以前试图聆听尸体的呓语声总是会感到头疼，期间会有很多杂乱的声音直接刺入他的脑神经。

但今天，不，就在刚才，那每每都会让他头疼不已的杂乱声竟然一点点消失了。

尸体的呓语声也变得更加清晰。

商非凡看到右眼视界中的进度条还没满，但小木屋里已经没有怨气让他吸收。

他转而看向尸体，还捏开尸体嘴巴闻了闻。手指也快速拂过死者头发，还取了死者一些指尖血。

治安官想提醒他不要破坏尸体，可老商动作太快，治安官还没来得及开口，他已经挤出血液装入小瓶中。

商非凡收起小瓶和用小袋子装起来的头发，转头问治安官：“尸体不用送去尸检吗？”

治安官想说的话被打断，局促道：“法医之前来看过，但他正忙着解剖那些巨虫。这次被毒死的巨虫有六只，我们这个街区只有他一位法医。因为那些巨虫的主人一直催，他只能先忙那边。”

治安官可能怕商非凡以为他和法医怠职，忙追补：“不过法医过来收集了死者的血液，化验分析后说是和毒死巨虫一样的毒-药，然后我们又在这间休息室的桌子上发现了死者留下的遗书……”

商非凡懂。看到遗书就偷懒地“断定”为自杀，也就不急着对死者进行尸检。

“遗书和毒-药呢？”

“这是重要证据，已经被搜证人员带走。”治安官忍不住问：“你看出什么了吗？”

商非凡没有回答治安官的问题，又问：“死者是直接吃下毒-药，还是喝下毒-药。毒-药是用什么东西盛装？”

治安官只能回答：“是喝下。死者把毒-药下在水杯里，喝到了肚子里。毒-药单独装在一个小纸袋里。”

“水杯呢？”

“也给搜证人员带走了。”

“水杯碎了吗？”

治安官回忆：“应该……没有。”

“水杯是什么材质？当时放在什么地方？”

“呃，应该是骨杯，放在……桌子上吧。”

“是倒下，还是正放？在桌子的哪个位置？”也许他应该尽快把照相机技术和影印技术给复制到这个世界。

“稍等，我先看看。”治安官对自己的记忆不太确定，翻开笔记本查看自己的记录，结果发现这些内容他都没有怎么记。

商非凡又问了几个问题。

治安官额头冒出汗水，一边翻看笔记本上的记录，一边和自己的记忆做斗争。

最后，商非凡对治安官说道：“我想看看那封遗书、死者喝水的水杯，还有毒-药，需要那位督查同意，对吗？”

治安官飞快点头，巴不得这个上面来的调查官能直接去找他的上司。

虎不帅那边结束“默哀”，抬起了头。

两人目光接触，默契地一起往外走。

治安官偷偷抹汗，只觉得商非凡果然不愧是上面派下来的调查官，这些来自特别调查局的调查官就没有一个简单的，他们就算没有人人觉醒神血天赋，也一定有常人没有的专业能力。别看人家只是进来大致看了一圈，说不定就看出了什么关键线索。

治安官偷偷地想，这个案子恐怕无法以自杀来结案了。当然，如果他们督查能坚持，还能得到大督查默许的话，那就另当别论。

可如果真是一个简单的案子，督查和大督查也没必要插手。如果他们非要插手，就说明……

治安官打了个冷颤，不敢再深想下去。

他就是普通的街区治安官，这辈子都不知道有没有升上去的可能，想那么多干嘛，上面让他怎么做他就怎么做就是。

刚从小木屋出来，治安官就被人叫走，似乎是赔偿额度没谈拢，死去的巨虫坐骑的主人们正在闹事。

虎不帅确定周围没有什么人，这才低声问商非凡：“你是不是有所发现？”

商非凡反问：“你呢？”

虎不帅犹豫片刻，点头：“死者并不是自杀，他被毒死时完全不知道发生了什么事情，只有痛苦和焦急和强烈的求生欲-望，但毒-药发作得非常快，他甚至来不及求救。我怀疑给巨虫下毒的人也不是他。这不是灭口，是给出一个凶手。”

“你能听到亡者的声音？”商非凡有一点点好奇。

虎不帅避开商非凡的目光直视，轻声回答：“不是亡者的声音，是尸体的呓语声。”

商非凡正想问两者有什么不同，就听虎不帅再次问他：“你的发现是什么？”

“这种毒-药发作速度很快，对吧？”商非凡不答反问。

“应该是。”

“我没有在死者的嘴巴里闻到食物的味道，也没有看到食物残渣，说明他应该是喝水中毒。治安官的回答也确认了这点。但是……如果你正在喝水，突然中毒且毫无心理准备，水杯会怎样？”

“落到地上或桌子上？也有可能因为激痛被握碎。”

商非凡给了一个赞许的眼神：“但我没有看到桌子和地面上有任何干涸的液体痕迹。当然这也不排除那液体发挥得特别快，且毫无杂质到干涸也不会留下痕迹。而杯子的材质是骨杯，也许这个骨杯特别结实才没有摔坏。对于这两点，我们等下去看看搜证人员带走的杯子就知道。

另外，死者是躺在床上的，双手还放在腹部，神态狰狞，姿势却很安详。这看起来是很像自杀，但……”

商非凡忽然伸手顺了下虎不帅的脑后头发，没碰到，就是做了个动作：“就算是自杀，死者的头发很短很硬，如果是他自己躺下，死时还比较痛苦，他的头发，尤其是后脑勺这里就不会很平整。但死者的后脑勺头发就很平整，就像是……”

“有人托着他的后脑勺，把他放到了床上。”虎不帅恍然接口。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 42: Galloping Full Speed Down the Path of a Villain (Part 1)

Shang Feifan suddenly felt an overwhelming wave of comfort wash over him. It felt as though someone suffering from severe hypoxia had suddenly been teleported to a natural oxygen bar sprawling across tens of thousands of acres of lush greenery. Every single breath he took made both his body and mind sing with pleasure.

A prompt popped up in his right eye: [Absorbing Grudge Energy.]

Below the text, a progress bar was slowly advancing.

Grudge energy? Shang Feifan raised a hand to rub his eyes. When he had first stepped inside, he had thought the room was merely dim, assuming the poor lighting was just an architectural flaw... So these wispy, dark threads floating before his eyes were actually grudge energy?

*Ding-dong.*

[Warning! Affected by dark energy, you are currently absorbing grudge energy. When you gaze long into the abyss, the abyss gazes also into you. Absorbing an excessive amount of dark energy will inevitably summon the dark self lurking deep within your soul. Proceed with extreme caution!]

Shang Feifan: Then how do I stop absorbing it passively? I already want to stop, but the grudge energy in this room is actively drilling into my body.

Besides, to be completely fair, absorbing this grudge energy genuinely felt even better than taking a sauna session.

Perhaps it was because his internal air purifier was working with such ruthless efficiency, but within moments, the lighting inside the small wooden cabin looked significantly brighter.

A flash of surprise crossed Hu Bushuai's eyes.

Whenever he had previously attempted to listen to the babbling murmurs of corpses, it always induced a splitting headache, with a chaotic jumble of voices piercing directly into his cerebral nerves.

Yet today—no, just moments ago—that chaotic clamor that never failed to torture him with blinding pain had vanished bit by bit.

Even the murmurs of the corpse grew far clearer.

Shang Feifan noticed that the progress bar in his right-eye vision was not yet full, but the small wooden cabin had run entirely out of grudge energy for him to absorb.

He shifted his attention instead to the corpse, even prying open its mouth to take a sniff. His fingers rapidly brushed across the dead man's hair, and he harvested a few fingertip blood samples from the deceased.

The bailiff wanted to warn him not to tamper with the body, but Lao Shang moved with such breathtaking speed that before the bailiff could even open his mouth, Shang Feifan had already squeezed out some blood and sealed it inside a tiny vial.

Shang Feifan tucked away the vial along with the hair, which he had stashed inside a small pouch, and turned to look at the bailiff. "Does the body not need to be sent for an autopsy?"

Interrupted mid-thought, the bailiff awkwardly stammered, "The coroner came by earlier, but he's up to his neck in giant bug dissections. There are six giant bugs that were poisoned to death this time, and our district only has one coroner. Since the owners of those giant bugs kept pushing and screaming, he had no choice but to deal with that side first."

Fearing that Shang Feifan might mistake him and the coroner for slackers, the bailiff hastily added, "However, the coroner did come over to collect the deceased's blood. After running tests and analysis, he said it was the exact same poison used on the giant bugs. Then we found a suicide note left behind by the deceased right here on the table in this breakroom..."

Shang Feifan understood. Upon seeing a suicide note, they lazily "concluded" it was a suicide, and thus felt no urgency to perform an autopsy on the dead man.

"Where are the suicide note and the poison?"

"Those are crucial pieces of evidence; the forensics team has already taken them away." The bailiff couldn't help asking, "Did you notice something?"

Shang Feifan ignored the bailiff's question and countered with another. "Did the deceased ingest the poison by eating it, or by drinking it? What kind of container held the poison?"

The bailiff could only reply, "He drank it. The deceased mixed the poison into a cup of water and drank it into his stomach. The poison itself was kept separately in a small paper bag."

"What about the cup?"

"Taken away by the forensics team as well."

"Was the cup broken?"

The bailiff tried to recall. "Should... should not be."

"What material was the cup made of? Where was it placed at the time?" Perhaps he ought to introduce photography and printing technology to this world as quickly as possible.

"Hold on, let me check." Unsure of his own memory, the bailiff flipped open his notebook to check his records, only to discover that he had hardly jotted down any of these details.

Shang Feifan rattled off a few more questions.

Beads of sweat popped up on the bailiff's forehead as he frantically flipped through his notebook while waging a desperate war against his own failing memory.

Finally, Shang Feifan said to the bailiff, "I'd like to take a look at that suicide note, the cup the deceased drank from, and the poison. I'll need the inspector's permission for that, right?"

The bailiff nodded rapidly, desperately wishing that this investigator from higher-ups would go straight to his superior.

Over by the side, Hu Bushuai finished his "moment of silence" and raised his head.

The two men exchanged a glance, and with tacit understanding, walked out together.

The bailiff secretly wiped the sweat from his brow. He figured that Shang Feifan truly lived up to his billing as an investigator dispatched from the upper echelons; none of these investigators from the Special Investigation Bureau were simple characters. Even if they hadn't all awakened divine bloodline talents, they undoubtedly possessed professional capabilities ordinary people lacked. Never mind that the man had just strolled in and taken a rough look around—who knew, he might have already spotted some crucial clues.

The bailiff thought to himself stealthily that this case would probably be impossible to close as a suicide now. Of course, if their inspector insisted on it and managed to get the tacit approval of the chief inspector, that would be a different story.

Yet if it were truly a simple case, the inspector and chief inspector wouldn't have needed to meddle in the first place. If they insisted on sticking their noses in, it meant...

The bailiff shuddered, daring not to let his thoughts wander any further down that road.

He was just an ordinary district bailiff; he didn't even know if he had a snowball's chance in hell of getting promoted in this lifetime. Why bother thinking about all this heavy stuff? He would just do whatever the higher-ups told him to do.

No sooner had they stepped out of the small wooden cabin than the bailiff was called away by someone—it seemed the compensation amounts had fallen through, and the owners of the dead giant-bug mounts were causing a ruckus.

Making sure there was no one in the immediate vicinity, Hu Bushuai lowered his voice and asked Shang Feifan, "Did you discover something?"

Shang Feifan deflected with a question of his own: "And you?"

Hu Bushuai hesitated for a brief second before nodding. "The deceased did not commit suicide. When he was poisoned, he had absolutely no idea what was happening. There was only pain, panic, and a fierce, desperate desire to survive, but the poison took effect so rapidly that he didn't even have time to cry out for help. I suspect he wasn't the one who poisoned the giant bugs either. This wasn't a silencing operation; it was a deliberate setup to pin the blame on a scapegoat."

"You can actually hear the voices of the dead?" Shang Feifan felt a flicker of curiosity.

Avoiding direct eye contact, Hu Bushuai replied in a soft voice, "Not the voices of the dead. The babbling murmurs of corpses."

Just as Shang Feifan was about to ask what the difference was, he heard Hu Bushuai ask him once more: "What were your discoveries?"

"This poison has an extremely fast acting time, doesn't it?" Shang Feifan answered a question with a question.

"It should."

"I didn't smell any food on the deceased's breath, nor did I see any food residue, which suggests he was poisoned by drinking water. The bailiff's answer confirmed this as well. But... if you were drinking water, were suddenly poisoned, and had zero psychological preparation, what would happen to the cup?"

"It would drop to the ground or the table? Or it might even be crushed in the grip of sudden, agonizing pain."

Shang Feifan shot him an approving look. "Yet I saw no dried liquid stains whatsoever on either the table or the floor. Of course, that doesn't rule out the possibility that the liquid evaporated exceptionally fast, leaving no trace behind even when dry, and possessing absolute purity. As for the cup, it was made of bone; perhaps this particular bone cup was exceptionally sturdy and didn't shatter. As for those two points, we'll know once we go down and inspect the cup taken away by forensics.

"In addition, the deceased was lying flat on the bed, with both hands resting on his abdomen. His expression was ferocious, yet his posture was serene. At a glance, it looks very much like suicide, but..."

Shang Feifan suddenly reached out to smooth down the hair at the back of Hu Bushuai's head. He didn't actually touch it, merely mimicking the motion in the air. "Even in suicide, the deceased's hair was short and coarse. If he had lain down by himself while experiencing such intense agony, his hair—especially right here at the back of his head—wouldn't be neatly arranged. But the hair at the back of the dead man's head was completely smooth, as if..."

"Someone was supporting the back of his head, gently laying him down onto the bed," Hu Bushuai seamlessly finished the thought with a sudden realization.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第42章 一路狂奔向反派的道路 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
商非凡收回手掌：“就是这样。他的手指也被人动过。死者的第一死亡地点并不是床，而是桌子前。桌子上有死者留下的新鲜爪尖抓痕，那应该是他中毒时的第一痛苦反应。可死者指甲缝里却没有木屑，这说明有人清理了他的指甲。”

布置自杀现场，他干过可不止一次。他们全都学习过怎么琢磨细节，包括不要把证据消除得太干净，因为这样反而会暴露很多。

“我们可以检查出指纹……”商非凡这句话说得很慢，看到虎不帅点头，就带着肯定语气说下去：“那个小木屋的桌子、床沿都太干净，被人特意来回擦拭过。可从死者的衣着打扮来看，他并不是一个很讲究洁净的人。”

商非凡总结：“谋杀死者的人勉强称得上是个专业人士，但很可能是个新手，而且是独自行动。”

虎不帅同意他的分析：“可这样我们依然无法找出真正的凶手是谁。且看治安官那边的态度，他们似乎急着结案，并不想深查下去。”

商非凡神秘一笑，“如果是今天之前，想要调查出真凶，可能真的要花一点时间。但你运气比较好，就在先前，我得到了一个馈赠，也许会对我们调查真凶有一定帮助。”

虎不帅也有自己的办法可以调查下去，但商非凡有能力且愿意帮忙，他也不会傻到说不用。

就是他有点搞不明白，对方为什么到现在都不和他相认。他不认识诺曼霍希尔很正常，可以他在王城和附属城某些阶层中的知名度，普通兽人不知道他也就算了，身为特别调查局调查官的诺曼霍希尔怎么可能也不认识他？

嗯，继续观察。

商非凡在坐骑休息区绕了一圈，找了个僻静角落，开始搞迷信活动。

虎不帅不知道他要做什么，就在一边看着。

狰爷饿了，跑到休息区食槽找食物吃。

药剂市场坐骑休息区闹出投毒事件，往常都要靠抢的休息区一下变得空荡许多，食槽那里更是不见坐骑踪影。

狰爷乐得一只虫霸占了全部食槽。

虎不帅还劝商非凡，这几天最好不要让巨虫在这里进食。

但商非凡问了狰爷，狰爷表示它已经记住那种毒-药的味道，以后它都会避开。

商非凡也去检查了食槽，现在那里被市场管理处好几个工作人员盯着，送出来的食物也变得更加新鲜。

老商想着有便宜不占白不占，加上狰爷自己乐意，就随它去了。

商非凡要搞迷信活动就不好再抱着阿呆，就让阿呆自己下地待着。

阿呆抬头看看虎不帅，一点点贴近他的小腿，嗅了嗅，停住不动。

虎不帅索性弯腰抱起阿呆。

“他很喜欢你。”实际上商非凡很担心阿呆会对虎不帅也张口喊爸。

不是他要跟虎不帅抢爸比这个职位，他只是不想虎不帅误会，误会他借幼崽碰瓷泡孩他爸。

“他很可爱。”虎不帅揉揉阿呆毛茸茸的方脑袋，看他眯着眼的小模样，觉得这孩子呆萌呆萌。

商非凡心想那是你没见到他两个月前叫丑又秃。

刚开始，虎不帅还很有兴趣地看商非凡在地上涂涂画画，但看着看着他的脸色就变了。

“你在干什么？”虎不帅小声轻问，一副不敢让附近人听到的小心样。

商非凡掏出装了死者血液的小瓶子以及装了死者头发的小袋子，常声回答：“我在让真凶自己跳出来。”

虎不帅警惕地往左右看看，往前略微跨了一步，弯腰，声音压得更小：“你……是不是学了一点很特别的知识？”

“算是吧。”商非凡头也不抬，在咒术阵的阵眼处滴下三滴血液。

虎不帅看着地面那怕别人不知道一样的大大“咒”字，特别想质问对方：“你哪来这么大的胆子，竟然敢在大庭广众之下施展咒术？”

他问出来了！

商非凡惊讶，抬头看青年：“不可以吗？”

虎不帅：“……你要是不想被人忌惮，也不想被治安官抓捕起来的话，最好快点抹除掉所有痕迹。”

自认为已经练出一颗大心脏的虎不帅这时也忍不住前后左右看，就怕有人注意到他们这里，然后走过来看到商非凡在干什么。

商非凡速度变快了一点：“好，知道了，马上就好。”

虎不帅：“……”我这是跟什么人混在一起了？

这家伙之前还被人诅咒得差点死了……他确认过对方的心跳和鼻息，当时这个虎兽人确实没了气息，但他都能魂穿第二次，有人只是暂时失去呼吸，然后被一个黑洞吸走，再安然无恙地冒出来，也很正常。

正常个鬼！

这家伙一身谜。

两个月不见，被诅咒死的人竟然学会了诅咒术。这点就超级不可思议！

如果诅咒术真那么好掌握，这个世界百分百会再毁灭一次——大家彼此诅咒就能把天河星的生物给诅咒灭绝。

也许对方只是装装样子？

就跟村里的羊大婶一样，她搞出的祭祀活动大多都只是个样子货，她自己承认，镇上所有人也都知道这点。

但商非凡搞出来的咒术阵是样子货吗？

商非凡掏出一枚面额为十的银达鲁放到祭品位，再把死者的头发烧成灰洒在咒术阵上，口中念咒：“一个喷嚏有人想，两个喷嚏有人骂。至高伟大的存在，诅咒之神科尼泽厄斯，您的信徒正在呼唤您。死者的血与身体化作的灰指引您的目光，死者在诅咒，诅咒害死他的人不断打喷嚏，直到凶手被抓到。”

虎不帅听到了商非凡不算太小声的咒语声，沉默了：这么儿戏的咒语真的能有效果吗？而且他还是第一次听说诅咒的献祭物竟然可以直接献上钱币，还只有十银，他就不怕诅咒之神看他不顺眼对他降下永久诅咒吗？不，诅咒之神根本不会理睬他。其实这家伙就是逗他玩呢吧？
chunks.englishText:
Shang Feifan withdrew his palm. "Precisely. His fingers had also been tampered with. The primary death scene of the deceased wasn't the bed; it was in front of the desk. There were fresh claw-tip scratch marks left by the deceased on the desk, which should have been his initial visceral reaction when the poison took hold. Yet there were no wood shavings lodged beneath the dead man's fingernails, indicating that someone had meticulously cleaned his nails."

Staging a suicide scene was a trick he had pulled off more than once. They had all been trained to obsess over minute details, including the wisdom against scrubbing evidence too clean, because doing so ironically exposed a mountain of flaws.

"We can check for fingerprints..." Shang Feifan dragged out the sentence deliberately. Seeing Hu Bushuai nod, he continued with an assured tone, "The desk and the bedframe in that small wooden cabin were far too spotless; someone had deliberately wiped them back and forth. Yet judging by the dead man's attire and grooming, he was hardly a neat freak."

Shang Feifan summarized, "Whoever murdered the deceased can barely qualify as a professional, but they are most likely an amateur, and they acted alone."

Hu Bushuai concurred with his analysis. "Even so, we still have no way of finding out who the real killer is. And judging by the bailiff's attitude, they seem desperate to close the case and have zero intention of digging deeper."

Shang Feifan smiled with a hint of mystery. "If it were before today, unearthing the true culprit might genuinely have taken some time. But you happen to be in luck—just a moment ago, I received a windfall, and it might just give us a helping hand in hunting down the real murderer."

Hu Bushuai had his own investigative channels, but since Shang Feifan had the capability and the willingness to lend a hand, he wasn't foolish enough to turn it down.

The only thing he couldn't quite wrap his head around was why this fellow still refused to acknowledge his identity. It was entirely normal if he didn't recognize Norman Hocheil, but given his own fame across certain circles in the Royal City and its vassal cities, ordinary beastmen not knowing him was one thing—how could Norman Hocheil, an investigator from the Special Investigation Bureau, possibly fail to recognize him?

Hmph, let's keep watching.

Shang Feifan took a stroll around the mount rest area, picked out a secluded corner, and launched into his superstitious rituals.

Unsure of what the man was up to, Hu Bushuai simply stood by and watched.

Master Zeng was hungry, so it scampered over to the feeding trough in the rest area to forage for food.

With the poisoning incident having shaken up the mount rest area of the potion market, the normally fiercely contested resting zone had instantly become vastly more deserted, and not a single mount was to be seen anywhere near the troughs.

Master Zeng was more than happy to monopolize the entire feeding trough all by its bugly self.

Hu Bushuai even tried to advise Shang Feifan that it would be best not to let the giant bug feed here for the next couple of days.

However, when Shang Feifan questioned Master Zeng, the bug indicated that it had already memorized the scent of that poison and would steer clear of it in the future.

Shang Feifan had also inspected the trough; it was currently being closely monitored by several staff members from the market management office, and the food being brought out had become noticeably fresher.

Lao Shang figured that failing to take advantage of freebies was a crime in itself, and since Master Zeng was willing, he let the bug do as it pleased.

Since Shang Feifan needed to conduct superstitious rituals, it wouldn't do to keep holding Dadao, so he let the little fellow down onto the ground to stand on its own two feet.

Dadao looked up at Hu Bushuai, inched closer to his calf step by step, gave a little sniff, and froze in place.

Without missing a beat, Hu Bushuai bent down and scooped Dadao up into his arms.

"He really likes you." In truth, Shang Feifan was utterly terrified that Dadao might open his mouth and address Hu Bushuai as "Daddy" as well.

It wasn't that he wanted to contest the position of daddy with Hu Bushuai; he simply didn't want Hu Bushuai to misunderstand—to suspect that he was using a cub as a prop to hit on the child's other parent.

"He's very cute." Hu Bushuai rubbed Dadao's fuzzy, square head. Seeing the little one's squinting, contented expression, he thought the child was endearingly foolish and adorable.

Shang Feifan muttered to himself: That's just because you didn't see him two months ago when he was ugly and bald.

At first, Hu Bushuai watched with keen interest as Shang Feifan scribbled and drew symbols on the ground, but as he watched on, his expression shifted.

"What are you doing?" Hu Bushuai asked in a low whisper, moving with the cautious air of someone terrified of letting nearby people overhear.

Shang Feifan pulled out the tiny vial containing the dead man's blood and the small pouch holding his hair, replying in a normal tone: "I'm making the real killer jump out on their own."

Vigilantly glancing left and right, Hu Bushuai took a slight step forward, hunched over, and dropped his voice even lower. "Did you... pick up some extremely unorthodox knowledge somewhere?"

"You could say that." Without even lifting his head, Shang Feifan dropped three drops of blood onto the focal center of the curse array.

Staring at the giant, ostentatious Chinese character for "Curse" scrawled on the ground as if begging the world to miss it, Hu Bushuai felt an overwhelming urge to interrogate him: "Where on earth do you get the sheer audacity to cast curse techniques out in broad daylight?"

And speak he did!

Shang Feifan looked up at the young man in astonishment. "Is there a problem?"

Hu Bushuai: "...If you don't want to become a public pariah or get hauled away by the bailiffs, you'd better wipe away every trace right now."

Even Hu Bushuai, who prided himself on having forged a heart of steel, couldn't help craning his neck backward, forward, and sideways, terrified that someone might notice them and stroll over to witness what Shang Feifan was up to.

Shang Feifan sped up his movements slightly. "Alright, got it. I'm almost done."

Hu Bushuai: "..." What kind of lunatic have I gotten myself mixed up with?

This guy had nearly been cursed to death not too long ago... Hu Bushuai had personally verified the man's heartbeat and respiration; back then, this feline beastman had genuinely stopped breathing. Yet if a guy could pull off a second soul transmigration, then someone temporarily losing their breath, getting sucked away by a black hole, and then popping right back out safe and sound was probably well within the realm of normalcy.

Normal my foot!

This guy was a walking enigma.

Two months had passed, and the man who was supposedly cursed to death had actually learned how to cast curses. That alone was utterly mind-boggling!

If curse techniques were truly that easy to master, this world would undoubtedly destroy itself a second time—everyone could just curse each other until every living creature on the Heavenly River Star was wiped out.

Perhaps the fellow was just putting on a show?

Much like Auntie Sheep in the village, whose sacrificial rituals were mostly just for show—a fact she openly admitted and everyone in town was well aware of.

Yet was Shang Feifan's curse array just for show?

Shang Feifan fished out a ten-silver-thaler banknote, placed it on the offering spot, burned the dead man's hair into ash, scattered it across the curse array, and chanted aloud: "A sneeze means someone misses you, two sneezes mean someone's cursing you. Supreme and majestic existence, the God of Curses Conizeus, your devout believer calls upon you. May the blood of the dead and the ash of his mortal frame guide your gaze; the deceased lays a curse—a curse that the one who murdered him shall sneeze incessantly until the culprit is dragged to light."

Having overheard Shang Feifan's not-so-quiet incantation, Hu Bushuai fell into a heavy silence. Can a spell as ridiculously childish as this actually work? Besides, this was the first time he had ever heard of a sacrificial offering for a curse consisting straight-up of cold, hard cash—and a mere ten silver thalers at that! Wasn't he afraid the God of Curses would take offense at his cheapness and slap him with a permanent curse? No, the God of Curses wouldn't even deign to acknowledge him. Was this guy actually just messing with him for a laugh?

chunks.chineseText:
第43章 找到凶手

一阵风刮过。

商非凡刚站起身，地上的咒术阵竟然瞬间变黑，包括献祭的钱币在内，所有东西都被变成灰烬。再被风一吹，了然无痕。

虎不帅瞪大眼睛。

他第一次看到咒术阵会有这种变化，不过他也是第一次看到咒术师施展咒术。

羊大婶祭祀完后，原本献上去的东西什么样，结束后还是什么样。如果是食物，大家还会当场分吃掉，美其名曰神灵赐予。

所以这么儿戏的咒术竟然真的成功了吗？

“有什么问题吗？”商非凡觉得虎不帅看他的眼神很有趣。

他并不知道自己第一次利用咒术阵施展咒术就能成功是件多么让人震惊的事情。对他来说，这就是游戏，游戏就是一键施法，他还亲手绘制了阵法图，怎么可能会不成功。

虎不帅掩藏起真实想法，问：“凶手如果不在附近怎么办？我们要怎么在这么大的城市里找一个不断打喷嚏的人？而且对方也有可能已经离开摩罗城。”

“是有这种可能。”商非凡伸手要接过阿呆：“不过绝大多数人都有表现心，当你完成一件你自认为还不错的作品时，除了想要给别人看到，也会希望看到听到别人对你作品的评价。尤其那个人还是个自认手艺上佳的新人。”

虎不帅忍住立刻观察周边有没有人打喷嚏的欲望：“你对人的心理很了解。”

“不，我只是赌运气而已。”商非凡一脸他也是凡人的淡然（装13）神情说：“但有很大的几率，为什么不尝试？如果这招不行，我们也可以再想其他办法。只不过浪费十个银达鲁而已。”

等找到真凶，他一定会把这笔花费从对方身上加倍收回。

人缺什么就会欣赏什么，虎不帅感觉自己有被商非凡帅到。

阿呆缩了缩，老商刚才干了啥，一股特别可怕的气息缠绕着他。他不想老商抱着他，但他也不敢拒绝……

两人搞完迷信活动就去了这个街区的治安办公楼。

商非凡打算找这里的督查要个可以查看证物的许可，如果能让他参与这个案件的调查最好。如果这个督查不好说话……他达到目的的手段很多，到时再说。

结果两人刚走到治安办公楼附近，就看到一个穿着治安员制服的年轻兽人一边打着喷嚏一边从办公楼大门里走出来。

他旁边还有一个中年兽人，两人看着像是搭档。

中年兽人很关心这位年轻搭档：“你怎么了？刚才就喷嚏不断，感冒了？”

“阿嚏！”年轻兽人捂住鼻子，“不是，就算感冒也不会这么连续打……阿嚏！阿嚏！”

中年兽人同情：“那就是过敏性鼻炎？要不要找个医师看看？”

“不用，也许过一会儿就……阿嚏！”年轻兽人捂着嘴巴和鼻子打了个大大的喷嚏。

中年兽人略微嫌弃地站远了一点。

“你这样可没办法工作。我看你还是先去找个医师或药师吧。”

年轻兽人想说话，但接二连三的喷嚏让他连句完整的话都说不出来。

虎不帅神色微妙。

商非凡抱着阿呆，静静地欣赏自己的杰作，还跟虎不帅咬耳朵：“你的运气真的很不错。对了，你知道吗，打喷嚏也会致使人死亡哦。”

虎不帅：“……他这样一看就不正常。”

“你觉得我像一名厉害的治疗祭司吗？”

“嗯？”虎不帅还没反应过来，就看商非凡已经抱着小幼崽走向那名年轻的治安员。

“日安，治安官先生们。这位情况看起来好像不太妙。”商非凡打招呼。

中年治安员看向商非凡，被老商那种成功人士的气质所惑，回礼：“日安，先生。是的，他这个情况有点糟糕，我正在劝他去看医师。”

商非凡距离年轻治安员两步远的地方停住，打量他，随后摇头：“他这个情况看医师可没什么用处。他这是被死者的怨念纠缠，被死人诅咒了。”

“什么？！”中年治安员变色，当即又往旁边退了一步。

可能觉得自己这个动作不太有同事情，中年治安员赶紧询问商非凡：“你是怎么看出来的？我的这位搭档真的被……”

“不可能！你胡……阿嚏阿嚏！”年轻治安员想要否认和斥责商非凡，但他根本无法开口说话。

虎不帅走近三人。

年轻治安员看到虎不帅，下意识挪开目光，随后就又是一连串的喷嚏打出。

商非凡用眼睛对虎不帅说：这小子显然认识你。

虎不帅也看出来了。对方就如商非凡所说还算不上老练，加上不停歇的打喷嚏也让他无力掩饰自己的真实神情。

“我很确定。我以前就见过类似的病例，而且他身上缠绕着死者的怨气，非常浓重，也非常……新鲜。”

中年治安员吞口水，不知为何，这个貌似神棍的兽人让他产生了莫名的恐惧心理，靠近这个人，他甚至听到了隐隐的凄厉嚎叫声。

中年治安员用力摇头，错觉！

神棍商面色冷厉，目光如刀地看向年轻治安员：“你刚害死了一个人，对方还是惨死，死者满腔怨愤无处宣泄，虽然这股怨气现在还只是让你打打喷嚏，但很快它就会侵蚀你的身体和灵魂，影响到你的健康和运势。甚至会影响到你周围的人，致使他们也生病和倒霉。”

你他妈胡扯！年轻治安员所有话语都被憋在一个接一个的喷嚏中，更可怕的是，他感觉自己被一只可怕的凶兽阴影给笼罩了。

中年治安员刚刚伸出去打算安慰自己同事的手，默默缩回，还又往旁边挪远了一点，嘴上却严厉地说：“这位先生，请不要乱说话！你这样的说法是对我同事的严重指责和侮辱，如果没有证据可以证明你的话，你就犯了诽谤罪。”

商非凡只瞥了一眼中年治安员，就把他镇住。他此时的气势太强，还毫无自知。

“是不是诽谤，就让死者来证明。”神棍商像是看到了别人看不见的网线。他转头看向药剂市场坐骑休息区方向，又看向年轻治安员。

年轻治安员愤怒抬头，与商非凡目光直接接触。

年轻治安员心脏猛地一颤。对方的目光太可怕，他发誓他从对方的眼睛中看到了最深的黑暗！

商非凡逼近一步：“你杀死的那个人的尸体距离这里并不远，想要证明你是否凶手也很简单，我甚至可以让怨魂重演你当时杀害他的全部过程……”

商非凡话音还没落，那名年轻治安员突然向与三人相反的方向冲逃了出去。

中年治安员愣住。

商非凡冷冷一笑，就这点抗压力还敢当坏蛋？随手把阿呆抛给虎不帅，抓起治安楼外面插着的旗杆，轻松拔起，甩手就投掷了出去。

咻！

“啊！”逃跑中的年轻治安员惨叫跌倒，瘸着一条腿爬起来还想跑。

中年治安员追了上去，他并没有立刻压制住年轻治安员，只质问他为什么要逃跑。

周围也有人注意到这一幕，有人围了过来。

Chapter 43: Finding the Culprit (Part 1)

A gust of wind swept past.

The moment Shang Feifan stood back up, the curse array on the ground instantly blackened. Everything within it, down to the banknote offered as sacrifice, was reduced to ash. A second later, another breath of wind blew through, leaving behind absolute, unblemished nothingness.

Hu Bushuai’s eyes widened.

This was the first time he had ever witnessed such a bizarre transformation in a curse array, though to be fair, it was also his first time seeing a curse master actually cast a curse.

Whenever Auntie Sheep finished a sacrificial ritual, whatever offerings had been placed on the altar looked precisely the same when it ended. If they were food items, everyone would even divvy them up and eat them on the spot under the fancy guise of "divine bestowal."

So... had a curse as childishly absurd as this actually succeeded?

"Is something the matter?" Shang Feifan found Hu Bushuai’s expression highly amusing.

He had no inkling of just how jaw-dropping a feat it was to pull off a successful spell using a curse array on his very first try. To him, this was just a game—and games were all about one-click spellcasting. He had personally drawn the ritual diagram himself; failure was mathematically impossible.

Concealing his genuine thoughts, Hu Bushuai asked, "What if the killer isn't nearby? How are we supposed to hunt down someone who won't stop sneezing in a massive city like this? Besides, there's a strong chance the culprit has already skipped town and left Moro City."

"That's certainly a possibility." Shang Feifan reached out to take Dadao back. "However, the overwhelming majority of people suffer from a deep-seated urge for validation. When you finish a piece of work that you consider to be quite a masterpiece, aside from wanting to show it off to others, you naturally yearn to see and hear what people have to say about it. Especially when the person in question fancies themselves a rookie with exceptional craftsmanship."

Hu Bushuai forcibly suppressed the sudden, overwhelming urge to scan his surroundings for anyone sneezing. "You understand human psychology remarkably well."

"Nah, I'm just playing the odds." With the detached, effortless nonchalance of a mortal who secretly fancied himself a god (flexing hard), Shang Feifan stated, "Since the probability is remarkably high, why not give it a shot? If this trick falls flat, we can always brainstorm other methods. At worst, we've only wasted ten silver thalers."

Once he tracked down the true culprit, he would most certainly squeeze every single copper back out of the bastard with interest.

People tended to admire whatever qualities they lacked. At that moment, Hu Bushuai felt like he had just been thoroughly dazzled by Shang Feifan's effortless cool.

Dadao cowered back. What on earth had Lao Shang just done? A terrifying, oppressive aura was clinging to the man like a shroud. He didn't want Lao Shang to hold him, yet he didn't dare refuse either...

Once their superstitious activities concluded, the pair headed straight for the district bailiff office.

Shang Feifan intended to hit up the local inspector for a permit to inspect the physical evidence, and if he could secure a spot participating in the case investigation, all the better. If this inspector proved uncooperative... well, he had plenty of methods up his sleeve to achieve his goals. They could cross that bridge when they came to it.

As it turned out, the moment the two men approached the vicinity of the bailiff's office, they spotted a young beastman clad in a bailiff's uniform stumbling out through the front doors, sneezing continuously.

Walking right beside him was a middle-aged beastman; judging by their demeanor, the pair looked to be partners.

The middle-aged beastman looked deeply concerned for his young partner. "What's wrong with you? You've been sneezing nonstop since a moment ago—did you catch a cold?"

"Achoo!" The young beastman clutched his nose. "No, even if I caught a cold, I wouldn't sneeze back-to-back like thi—achoo! Achoo!"

The middle-aged beastman offered a sympathetic look. "Could it be allergic rhinitis, then? Do you want to go see a physician?"

"No need, maybe it'll stop in a bit—achoo!" Muffling his mouth and nose, the young beastman unleashed a massive sneeze.

With a hint of unspoken disgust, the middle-aged beastman took a cautious step backward.

"You're in no condition to work like this. I suggest you go find a physician or a apothecary first."

The young beastman opened his mouth to reply, but a relentless barrage of sneezes choked off any chance of forming a coherent sentence.

Hu Bushuai wore a peculiar expression.

Cradling Dadao in his arms, Shang Feifan quietly stood back to admire his own handiwork, leaning in to whisper in Hu Bushuai's ear: "Your luck is seriously top-notch. By the way, did you know? Sneezing can actually be fatal, you know."

Hu Bushuai: "...Anyone can tell he's acting abnormal."

"Do you think I look like a formidable healing priest?"

"Huh?" Before Hu Bushuai could even process the question, he watched Shang Feifan stride forward with the little cub straight toward the young bailiff.

"Good day, gentlemen of the bailiff's office. This young man here doesn't look so hot," Shang Feifan greeted smoothly.

The middle-aged bailiff turned his attention to Shang Feifan, instantly taken in by Lao Shang's aura of a successful elite, and returned the greeting. "Good day, sir. Indeed, his condition is rather dismal; I was just trying to talk him into seeing a physician."

Stopping a mere two paces away from the young bailiff, Shang Feifan looked him up and down before slowly shaking his head. "Seeing a physician isn't going to do him a lick of good. This fellow's been entangled by the deep-seated grievances of the deceased. He's been cursed by a dead man."

"What?!" Color drained from the middle-aged bailiff's face, and he instinctively recoiled another step.

Realizing that this action looked rather unsupportive of his colleague, the middle-aged bailiff hastily questioned Shang Feifan, "How could you tell? Has my partner really been..."

"Impossible! You're talking nonse—achoo, achoo!" The young beastman tried his best to deny and chew out Shang Feifan, but he couldn't form a single coherent word.

Hu Bushuai closed the distance, joining the three of them.

Upon catching sight of Hu Bushuai, the young bailiff reflexively averted his gaze, only for another relentless string of sneezes to violently wrack his body.

Shang Feifan telegraphed a look to Hu Bushuai: *This kid clearly knows you.*

Hu Bushuai had caught it too. As Shang Feifan had noted, the fellow was far too green, and the unyielding onslaught of sneezes stripped away any lingering ability to mask his true reactions.

"I am quite certain of it. I've encountered similar clinical cases before, and the lingering grudge energy attached to him is intensely thick, exceptionally heavy, and... remarkably fresh."

The middle-aged beastman swallowed hard. For some inexplicable reason, this charlatan-looking beastman was instilling an eerie sense of dread in him; standing close to this guy made him fancy he could hear faint, mournful wails echoing in the air.

Violently shaking his head, the middle-aged beastman dismissed the thought: *An optical illusion!*

With a chilling, stern expression, the charlatan Shang fixed a razor-sharp gaze upon the young bailiff. "You just snuffed out a human life, and a miserable death at that. The victim burns with unvented rage and grievance with nowhere to outlet it. While this malice is currently content to merely make you sneeze, it will soon devour your flesh, corrode your soul, and wreck your health and fortune. It might even bleed over to the people around you, dragging them down into sickness and misfortune."

*You're fucking talking out of your ass!* Every single retort the young beastman wanted to hurl was choked back by a fresh volley of explosive sneezes. What terrified him even more was the crushing sensation that he had just been swallowed whole by the shadow of a terrifying beast of prey.

The middle-aged bailiff silently retracted the hand he had half-extended to comfort his colleague, shuffling a few paces further away while maintaining a stern front. "Sir, please refrain from spouting nonsense! Accusations of this magnitude are a grave slander and insult against my partner. If you lack solid evidence to back up your claims, you're looking at a criminal charge of defamation."

Glancing sideways at the middle-aged beastman, Shang Feifan managed to instantly freeze him in his tracks with a single look. His dominating presence at that moment was completely effortless, radiating an intensity he wasn't even consciously aware of.

"Whether it's slander or not, let the deceased speak the truth." The charlatan Shang, acting as if he could perceive invisible ley lines threading through the air, shifted his gaze from the mount rest area back toward the young bailiff.

Furious, the young bailiff snapped his head up, locking eyes directly with Shang Feifan.

A sharp jolt stabbed through the young bailiff's heart. The man's gaze was entirely too terrifying; he swore he caught a glimpse of the deepest, darkest abyss lurking within those eyes!

Shang Feifan closed in by a single step. "The corpse of the man you murdered isn't far from here. Proving whether you're the killer is child's play—I can even make the vengeful spirit replay every single detail of how you murdered him..."

Before Shang Feifan could even finish his sentence, the young bailiff abruptly wheeled around and bolted in the opposite direction.

The middle-aged bailiff froze in sheer bewilderment.

With a cold, mocking smirk, Shang Feifan thought: *And this lightweight thinks he has the guts to play the villain?* Casually tossing Dadao over to Hu Bushuai, he reached out, effortlessly yanked up the flagpole planted outside the bailiff's station, and hurled it with a casual flick of his wrist.

*Swish!*

"Agh!" The fleeing young bailiff let out a miserable shriek, tumbling hard to the ground. Dragging a shattered, hobbling leg, he scrambled back up, desperate to keep running.

The middle-aged bailiff snapped out of his stupor and gave chase, though instead of immediately tackling the suspect, he merely bellowed after him, demanding to know why he was running away.

Passersby on the street began to notice the commotion, and a crowd slowly started to gather.

chunks.chineseText:
年轻治安员想要辩解，但他嘴巴刚张开就是不断的喷嚏声。

喷嚏震动身体，加剧了断腿的剧痛。年轻治安员疼得惨叫连连，又不断的打喷嚏，恶性循环。

“治安官先生，你的同伴现在很可疑，不把他抓起来吗？”商非凡冷眼看向中年治安员。

中年治安员为难。

年轻治安员眼泪鼻涕流满脸，张口：“我没有……阿嚏阿嚏！”

“没有杀人，你为什么逃跑？”商非凡声音异常冷酷。

年轻治安员只觉得自己像是真的被怨气纠缠住，他感觉自己被一股看不见的恐惧给笼罩，而恐惧的根源就来自面前这个质问他的兽人。

阿呆紧紧贴住虎不帅，他有点怕现在的老商。

“我……”

商非凡抓起地上旗杆，一杆子把人抽晕。

中年治安员惊：“你干什么！”

“日常见义勇为，不谢。”商非凡抬起下巴，示意中年治安员：“不把人先抓起来吗？上报、疗伤、审问，你的事情很多。另外，请查查这附近有没有人死亡，应该刚死不久。”

中年治安员抓住胸前挂着的勺子。

商非凡故意：“如果有需要，我可以帮你们找到那具尸体。”

中年治安员当然知道这附近刚死了人，药剂市场投毒事件闹得这么大，附近的治安员几乎都知道了。据说投毒者已经自杀，他们以为这个案子已经了结，没想到……

中年治安员到底含住了警哨，吹响。

没一会儿，治安楼里跑出好几个治安员。

中年治安员抬手示意。

“发生了什么事？咦，弗兰克怎么了？被人打伤了吗？”

几个治安员搞不清楚事情，纷纷询问。

中年治安员神情纠结：“先把人抬到局里，找个单间把他……关起来，再给他找个能接骨的医师，事情有点复杂。我会向上面禀报。”

几个治安员面面相觑，但还是依吩咐办事。

中年治安员看向商非凡：“这位先生，我需要你也一起走一趟。”

“走吧。”商非凡比他还干脆，还主动领头走向那栋治安楼。

半个小时后，商非凡与虎不帅一起见到了这个街区最大的治安官，三级督查，文德立。

文德立已经验证过商非凡的身份骨牌，沉默地把骨牌交还给商非凡，沉默地坐在办公桌后面，半天没有说话。

商非凡见多了这种场合，也知道这位文督查是想借用这种方式来对他进行心理压制，对此……他只是左腿架在右腿上，坐在办公桌对面的沙发里，眼神冷锐地看向文督查。

那架势看起来比真正的办公室主人还像做主的那个。

文督查暗中吸气。猜测对面的虎兽人很可能大有来头，也许他的身份不止是一名三级调查官，甚至有可能是一名贵族子弟，还是家里掌握了军政大权的大贵族家里排位比较靠前的继承人。

虎不帅抱着阿呆也坐在一边，不过他的气势就平淡多了，不注意，甚至会忽略他的存在。

阿呆脑袋一缩，更是毫无存在感。

文督查自感气势比不过对面，也被办公室内的沉默压得难受，率先打破沉寂：“诺曼霍希尔调查官，我能知道你来我们摩罗城是有着什么任务吗？这个任务又是否与药剂市场的投毒案有关？”

商非凡：“详细任务内容无法告知。我也是偶然碰到了这个投毒和疑凶疑似自杀的案件。”

文督查才不相信这是偶然。

“霍希尔调查官，明人不说暗话，我们来说说被你揭发和打伤的那名我的手下。你有什么证据证明他就是杀死药剂市场坐骑休息区负责人的凶手？”

“他承认了吗？”商非凡反问。

文督查：“正在审问。他喷嚏不断，说话不便，医师怀疑他得了某种奇怪的疾病。”

“诅咒。”商非凡冷冷吐出一词。

文督查噎住，“这种迷信的事情……”

“迷信？”商非凡似笑非笑：“这明明就是一种能量的运用方式。就像你手上戴着可以辅助你血脉天赋发挥的炼金戒指。”

“这么说你真的看到了死者怨魂纠缠在弗兰克身上？”文督查摸着戒指，忍不住问。

商非凡答非所问：“想要找到弗兰克投毒和栽赃嫁祸杀人的证据并不难。先查他和死者的关系，是否有私人仇恨。再查他和药剂市场的关系，是否有利益纠葛以及私人仇恨。同时再查他的收入，看他最近是否有大笔意外之财入手。四查……”

商非凡最后道：“当然，这些查案手法，我相信你们不比我陌生。我也相信你们一定有办法从那个弗兰克嘴里问出真相。”

“……”文督查一开始的气势被压制住，搞到现在他都无法露出强硬态度，他甚至有点头疼也有点恐惧自己会不会惹上麻烦。

这种特别调查局派出调查官到下属城市调查的事情，从来都不会是小事。

现在，他只希望这真的是一件简单的经济或私人仇恨案件，而没有牵扯到某些大人物和上面的斗争中。

“我们会尽全力调查清楚这件事。”文督查只能给出保证。

商非凡：“我相信你们的工作能力。不过在这之前，我希望能给我半个小时的时间和那位弗兰克先生独处。”

希望那位弗兰克先生是个聪明人。真的很笨也没什么，他相信他一定有办法让对方开口。拷问是一门艺术，而他的艺术水平还不错？

文督查犹豫：“他现在是嫌疑犯，但还没有实际证据可以证明他真的犯罪。独处不可能，必须有我们的人在场。”

商非凡笑了笑，“可以。谁都可以在场，只要他不介意自己听到的内容。”

文督查：“……”

文督查在心中破口大骂给他惹事的下属弗兰克。同时也越发肯定药剂市场投毒一事一定另有隐情，而且牵扯一定很深。

他想他需要跟他的顶头上司聊聊。

文督查自始至终都没怎么太注意坐在一边的虎不帅，他每次想要打量这个人，都会被商非凡引走注意力。

一直到两人离开，文督查才想起来办公室里还坐了这么一号人，对方还抱着一个小幼崽。

有人敲门，一颗大脑袋探进来：“督查？”

“什么事？”文督查不快喝问。

大脑袋推开门，干咳一声：“外面那个人说让我们给他准备一个单间，他要单独询问弗兰克一些话。说是您同意了？”

文督查沉默数秒：“给他准备。”

又加重语气：“单间。不要安排任何人偷看偷听。”

大脑袋面色一凛，迅速立正行礼：“是。”

办公室门被带上，文督查思考片刻，抽出一张信纸，沾了沾墨水，开始写信。

信件内容不长，写好后装入一支手指长的骨筒中。

打开窗户，吹出一声口哨。

一只背着邮递包的大鸟快速飞来。

文督查把密封的信件和送信费交给快递员：“尽快送达！”

大鸟看清送信地址及收件人，张口说人话：“第二街区，警监办公室，保证一个小时送到。”
chunks.englishText:
The young security officer wanted to defend himself, but the moment he opened his mouth, another fit of violent sneezing interrupted him.

The force of the sneezes wracked his entire body, aggravating the agonizing pain of his broken leg. Screaming in torment while simultaneously sneezing uncontrollably, the young officer was trapped in a vicious cycle.

"Officer, your companion is acting extremely suspicious right now. Aren't you going to arrest him?" Shang Feifan cast a cold glance at the middle-aged security officer.

The middle-aged officer was placed in a difficult position.

With tears and snot streaming down his face, the young officer managed to force out: "I didn't... *Achoo! Achoo!*"

"If you didn't commit murder, why did you run away?" Shang Feifan's voice was exceptionally chilling.

The young officer truly felt as though he had been entangled by lingering malice. He sensed himself enveloped by an invisible terror, the root of which emanated entirely from the beastman interrogating him before him.

A-Dai pressed tightly against Hu Bushuai, feeling somewhat afraid of Old Shang in his current state.

"I..."

Shang Feifan snatched up a flagpole from the ground and knocked the fellow unconscious with a single sweep of the pole.

The middle-aged security officer cried out in alarm: "What do you think you're doing?!"

"Just performing a daily act of civic courage. No need to thank me." Shang Feifan raised his chin, gesturing toward the middle-aged officer. "Aren't you going to arrest him first? Filing reports, providing medical treatment, interrogation—you have plenty to keep you busy. In addition, please check if anyone has died in this vicinity recently; it should have happened not long ago."

The middle-aged officer instinctively grasped the spoon hanging from his chest.

Shang Feifan intentionally provoked: "If necessary, I can help you find that corpse."

Naturally, the middle-aged officer was well aware that someone had just died nearby. The poison-spiking incident at the potion market had caused such a massive uproar that nearly all the local security officers knew about it. Word had it that the poisoner had already committed suicide; they thought the case had been closed, but who could have expected...

Ultimately, the middle-aged officer brought a police whistle to his lips and blew hard.

A moment later, several security officers rushed out from the security building.

The middle-aged officer raised a hand to signal them.

"What's going on here? Well, what happened to Frank? Was he beaten and injured by someone?"

Puzzled by the situation, several of the security officers voiced their questions.

With a conflicted expression, the middle-aged officer ordered, "Carry him into the station first, find a private room to... lock him up, and find an osteopath who can set bones. Things are a bit complicated. I'll report this to my superiors."

The officers exchanged glances, but still proceeded to carry out the orders.

The middle-aged officer looked at Shang Feifan. "Sir, I need you to come along with me as well."

"Let's go." Shang Feifan was even more decisive than the officer, taking the initiative to lead the way toward the security building.

Half an hour later, Shang Feifan and Hu Bushuai met the highest-ranking security officer of this district, Third-Class Inspector Wen Deli.

Wen Deli had already verified Shang Feifan's identity token. Silent, he handed the token back, sat quietly behind his desk, and said nothing for a long time.

Shang Feifan had seen plenty of such situations. He knew this Inspector Wen was attempting to use psychological pressure through this silence. As for this tactic... he merely crossed his left leg over his right, sat back in the sofa opposite the desk, and cast a cold, sharp gaze at the inspector.

That posture made him look far more like the master of the office than the actual person in charge.

Inspector Wen secretly drew a deep breath. He guessed that the tiger beastman opposite him likely had a formidable background. Perhaps his status went beyond a mere Third-Class Investigator; he could even be the scion of a noble family—an heir holding a relatively high ranking within a major aristocratic clan that wielded immense military and political power back home.

Holding A-Dai, Hu Bushuai also sat to the side, though his presence was far more understated. If one wasn't paying attention, they might even overlook his existence entirely.

A-Dai shrank his head back, making his presence feel even more negligible.

Sensing that his aura fell short of his opponent's and feeling suffocated by the heavy silence in the office, Inspector Wen broke the quiet first: "Investigator Norman Hochschild, might I ask what mission brings you to our Molo City? And does this mission have anything to do with the potion market poisoning case?"

Shang Feifan replied, "The details of my mission cannot be disclosed. I merely stumbled upon this case of poisoning and the suspected suicide of the prime suspect by coincidence."

Inspector Wen certainly didn't believe it was a coincidence.

"Investigator Hochschild, let's dispense with the pleasantries. Let's talk about my subordinate whom you exposed and beat up. What evidence do you have to prove he is the culprit who murdered the person in charge of the potion market's mount resting area?"

"Did he confess?" Shang Feifan countered with a question of his own.

Inspector Wen answered, "He is currently being interrogated. He keeps sneezing incessantly and has difficulty speaking. The physician suspects he has contracted some strange illness."

"A curse," Shang Feifan spat out coldly.

Inspector Wen choked on his words. "Superstitious nonsense like that..."

"Superstitious?" Shang Feifan wore a half-smile. "This is clearly a method of utilizing energy. Just like the alchemical ring you wear on your finger that assists in unleashing your bloodline talent."

"So you're saying you actually saw the vengeful spirit of the deceased entangling Frank?" Stroking his ring, Inspector Wen couldn't help asking.

Sidestepping the question, Shang Feifan said, "Finding evidence that Frank poisoned, framed, and murdered someone isn't difficult. First, investigate his relationship with the deceased to see if there was any personal grudge. Second, check his connection to the potion market to see if there were any conflicts of interest or personal grievances. At the same time, examine his income to see if he recently came into a large sum of unexpected wealth. Third..."

Shang Feifan concluded, "Of course, I believe you are no more a stranger to these investigative methods than I am. And I trust you certainly have ways to extract the truth from that fellow Frank."

"..." Inspector Wen's initial imposing momentum had been suppressed to the point where he couldn't even put on a tough facade anymore. He even felt a mild headache and a lurking fear that he might have waded into deep trouble.

Whenever the Special Investigation Bureau dispatched investigators to subordinate cities, it was never a trivial matter.

Right now, he only hoped this truly was a simple case of economic or personal grievance, untainted by the struggles between big shots and higher-ups.

"We will do our utmost to investigate this matter thoroughly," Inspector Wen could only offer this guarantee.

Shang Feifan stated, "I trust your professional competence. However, before that, I hope to be granted half an hour of solitude with Mr. Frank."

Hopefully, that Mr. Frank was a smart man. Even if he was truly a fool, he believed he definitely had ways to make the fellow talk. Interrogation was an art, and his artistic proficiency wasn't bad at all, right?

Hesitating, Inspector Wen said, "He is currently a suspect, but there is no actual evidence to prove he truly committed a crime. Total solitude is out of the question; some of our people must be present."

Shang Feifan chuckled. "Very well. Anyone can be present, as long as they don't mind hearing what's about to be said."

Inspector Wen: "..."

Internally, Inspector Wen cursed Frank, the subordinate who had brought this calamity upon him. At the same time, he became increasingly certain that the potion market poisoning incident held hidden depths and profound entanglements.

He felt he needed a chat with his direct superior.

From beginning to end, Inspector Wen hadn't paid much attention to Hu Bushuai sitting off to the side. Every time he attempted to size up that person, his attention would be deftly diverted by Shang Feifan.

It wasn't until the two of them left that Inspector Wen remembered such a person had been sitting in his office all along, holding a small cub no less.

Someone knocked on the door, and a large head poked inside: "Inspector?"

"What is it?" Inspector Wen demanded impatiently, his tone displeased.

Pushing the door open, the large-headed officer gave a dry cough. "The man outside said we should prepare a private room for him so he can question Frank in private. He claimed you approved it?"

Inspector Wen fell silent for several seconds. "Prepare it for him."

He added with a heavier tone, "A single room. Do not arrange for anyone to spy or eavesdrop."

The officer's expression tightened, and he quickly stood at attention and saluted: "Yes!"

The office door closed. Inspector Wen pondered for a moment, pulled out a sheet of stationery, dipped his pen in ink, and began to write.

The letter was not long. Once finished, it was tucked into a finger-length bone cylinder.

Opening the window, he let out a sharp whistle.

A large bird carrying a mail pouch rapidly flew over.

Inspector Wen handed the sealed letter and delivery fee to the courier: "Deliver this as quickly as possible!"

The large bird recognized the delivery address and recipient, and opened its beak to speak in human tongue: "Second District, Chief Inspector's Office. Guaranteed delivery within one hour."

chunks.chineseText:
大鸟刚刚带着信件飞走，文督查还没有关上窗户。

咚咚的紧急敲门声响起，办公室外一道熟悉的嗓音同时在喊：“督查，出事了！弗兰克死了。”

文督查……用力关上窗户。

商非凡和虎不帅迟了一步。

刚有治安员过来通知他们，说安排好了单间，让他们去见弗兰克。

可等他们打开房门，就看到弗兰克已经口吐黑色血液的死在了单间内。

幸好给他们开门的治安员也在，否则这事还真的有点说不清楚。
chunks.englishText:
CHINESE SOURCE TEXT (第43章 找到凶手 (Part 3)):
The large bird had just flown off with the letter, and Inspector Wen hadn't even closed the window yet.

Urgent, heavy knocking pounded against the door, and a familiar voice shouted from outside the office: "Inspector, something's happened! Frank is dead."

Wen Deli... slammed the window shut with force.

Shang Feifan and Hu Bushuai were a step too late.

An officer had just come to inform them that the solitary cell was ready and led them to see Frank.

But when they pushed open the door, they found Frank already dead inside the cell, dark blood spilling from his mouth.

Fortunately, the officer who opened the door for them was right there, otherwise this matter really would have been impossible to explain clearly.
"""

chunks.chapterTitle: 第44章 诅咒直线和郁闷的谷主 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第44章 诅咒直线和郁闷的谷主

商非凡站在单间门口，右眼视界陡然变红。

【警告！你正在被人诅咒！】

一行文字加大加粗出现，不是系统，是融入他右眼的玻璃球在提醒他，现在这玩意很可能还融合了他的诅咒技能。

又是诅咒？

他好像和诅咒特别有缘分。

【吞噬诅咒，还是驱散诅咒？】

商非凡在脑中想着“我要找到诅咒我的人”。

【吞噬诅咒，你会跟着诅咒之线找到诅咒你的人。】

商非凡立刻选择吞噬诅咒。

随后商非凡看到了一幕非常形象的动画，他看到一只拥有黑红色皮毛的小虎崽从他身体里冲出，一个虎跃，一口咬住一团像是线团的黑色雾气，没有立刻吞下，而是玩耍一般咬住又吐出，如此重复数次，才啊呜一口吞入腹中。

小虎崽满足地打了个滚，转头就回归他的身体。

而他的右眼看到了一条清楚的黑色线条延伸向远方。

商非凡点赞，这个诅咒祭司的技能真实惠又好用！

距离治安办公楼不远的药剂市场，一名正在行走的行人突然哇地喷出一口鲜血，把路人吓了一大跳。

行人捂住嘴唇，脸色苍白地快速离开药剂市场。

喷到地上的血液变成点点斑痕，斑痕中似乎混杂着一个又一个小黑点，但没有人注意到，一开始还有人特意避开这滩血迹，没多久就有人直接踩了上去。

血迹和混杂在血迹中的黑点很快就变成了城市尘土的一份子。

治安楼单间门口。虎不帅和听到惊叫跑过来的几个治安员都没有发现商非凡身上的变化，只有阿呆又往虎不帅的怀里缩紧了一些。

“弗兰克怎么了？”

有治安员想要进入单间，被商非凡拦住。

那治安员正要发火。

商非凡冷声：“冲进去破坏现场吗？在外面等着！”

几名治安员被老商气势镇住，眼睁睁看着商非凡和虎不帅进入单间。

“别乱来。弗兰克的死亡不简单，让那两人进去，这件事我们最好不要沾手。”经验丰富的老治安员压低声音对其他几个治安员说。

这话一出，原本愤愤不平的几个治安员也不说话了。

一进入单间，商非凡和虎不帅两人就互看一眼。

事情开始变质。

如果说毒杀巨虫坐骑只是为了恶心人，再毒杀休息区负责人进行栽赃嫁祸是贵族的傲慢——就是我干的，但你能拿我怎样。

可当被幕后者收买的治安员弗兰克也被毒杀后，事情就变得不那么简单。

不是幕后者做不到，而是不值得，如果这真的只是一个针对虎不帅的恶作剧。

弗兰克仰面倒在地上，两眼圆睁，死不瞑目，除了口鼻流血，他的手里虚握着一个瓶子，瓶口打开，里面的毒液已经流出大半。

看起来这又是一个自杀现场。

但诅咒的根源并不在弗兰克身上，不但不是，他还只是一个祭品，一个为了让诅咒成功而被献祭的生命。

商非凡看到浓厚的、不甘的、疯狂的怨气在弗兰克身上盘旋。

但这次他没有主动吸收，而是任由那些怨气一点点主动投入他的身体。

右眼视界中的怨气吸收进度条再次跳出，同样缓慢增加中。

商非凡不知道这个进度条有什么作用，似乎只是提醒他怨气吸收了多少。

如果进度条达到顶端会有怎样变化？

叮咚。

系统提醒他完成了任务五十一，得到了5个贡献点。

紧跟着系统又发布了新任务。

【任务五十二，摩罗城第六街区治安办公室发生疑似自杀的案件，请调查死者弗兰克是否死于自杀。给出判断后奖励1点贡献点。】

这个任务倒是比较好完成，他可以立刻给出答案，但在这之前，商非凡看向了虎不帅。

虎不帅正在垂眸聆听。

“保护现场！所有人都不准进去！”文督查厉喝声传来，亲自赶到。

围在单间门口的治安员散开。

文督查脚步在外面停顿了一下，这才进入单间。

他头疼！

这个死掉的弗兰克身份并不简单。

他是彘庞男爵长子彘圭的跟班之一，一年前拿着彘庞男爵的推荐信来到治安局工作。因为他自己从不隐瞒，甚至是炫耀他和彘庞男爵长子的关系，这片街区的治安员都知道他的身份底细。

弗兰克也确实到死之前都在帮彘圭做事。

之前听说上面来的调查官竟然抓住了弗兰克，还怀疑他毒杀药剂市场休息区负责人进行栽赃嫁祸，他就在心中大喊不妙。

没想到更不妙的事情发生了，弗兰克竟然死在了他们的办公地点内。

他现在只希望这件事和彘圭无关，更和彘庞男爵无关。

“畏罪自杀？”文督查也干过一线工作，扫过弗兰克的死亡现场，他做出了初步判断。

商非凡带了一点讽刺地笑：“你很想这么结案？”

文督查抿了抿嘴唇，尽量维持自己的督查尊严：“请注意你的说话方式，霍希尔先生。我们等级平级。”

他是三级督查，理论上他的等级和三级调查官等同。

但那只是理论，实际上特别调查局的调查官向来见官大一级，如果他们拿着密令，那就更不得了。

这也是文督查对商非凡客气的原因。

商非凡好笑，他根本无意压制文督查，但对方显然把他当敌人看了。就算不是敌人，也是来找麻烦的人。

虎不帅恰在此时抬头，对商非凡摇头：“不是自杀，有人逼迫他，毒-药也是对方交给他的。”

文督查听到了，立刻问：“你怎么知道？你发现了什么？”

虎不帅只是淡淡回复：“我的天赋能力，让我可以听到死者死后留下的呓语声。通常这些呓语也是死者记忆最清楚和最刻骨铭心的事情。”

“所以你无法给出明确证据。”文督查神情严厉。

虎不帅视如不见，“我只负责说出我的判断，找出死者的真实死亡原因和幕后凶手是你们治安官的事情。”

文督查深深看了眼虎不帅，心想这人的能力对于调查案件倒是很有用处，可惜不是他的手下。

文督查以为虎不帅也是特别调查局的人，或者就是商非凡请来帮忙的人。他更偏向于后者，因为没有哪个调查官在出来办案时还带着一只幼崽，除非那幼崽也有非常特别的能力。

“这是一个被自杀案件。”商非凡对系统说出自己的判断。

听到文督查的耳朵里，还以为是说给他听的。

“我们这里不是什么民间侦探组织，也不是某个祭司说什么就是什么的愚昧乡村。无论是什么结论，必须要有证据做支撑。”

文督查慷锵有力地扔出这句话，当即转头命令门口看热闹的调查员：“让搜证处的技术人员立刻过来！另外这个案子将由巴特亲自负责。”

“是。”被点名的老治安官脸色不变地走出来，实际满腹苦水。

商非凡拉住虎不帅的手，往后退了两步，摆出他们无意插手调查的态度。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 44: The Curse's Trajectory and the Gloomy Valley Master

Standing at the entrance of the private room, Shang Feifan's right field of vision suddenly turned crimson.

[Warning! You are currently being cursed!]

A line of bold, enlarged text appeared. It wasn't the system, but the glass orb fused into his right eye reminding him. By now, this item had likely also integrated his Curse skill.

Another curse?

He seemed to have a particularly deep affinity with curses.

[Devour the curse, or dispel the curse?]

Shang Feifan thought within his mind, "I want to find the person who cursed me."

[By devouring the curse, you will follow the curse's thread to find its caster.]

Shang Feifan instantly chose to devour the curse.

Immediately afterward, Shang Feifan witnessed a vivid animation. He saw a small tiger cub with black-and-red fur burst out from his body, leaping forward to clamp its jaws onto a ball of black mist resembling a tangle of yarn. Instead of devouring it immediately, the cub playfully bit and spat it out, repeating this several times before swallowing it down with a satisfied "nom."

The tiger cub rolled over contentedly, turned around, and returned into his body.

Meanwhile, his right eye perceived a distinct black line extending far into the distance.

Shang Feifan gave a mental thumbs-up—this Curse Priest skill was practically a steal, extremely useful!

Over at the potion market not far from the security building, a pedestrian walking along suddenly vomited a mouthful of blood, giving nearby passersby a massive fright.

Clamping a hand over his mouth, the pedestrian hurriedly fled the potion market with a pale face.

The blood splattered on the ground formed tiny spots, within which seemed to mingle minuscule black dots. Yet no one noticed; while a few people initially deliberately avoided this patch of blood, before long, others stepped right on top of it.

The bloodstains and the black dots mixed within them quickly became part of the city dust.

At the entrance of the security cell, neither Hu Bushuai nor the security officers who had rushed over at the sound of the cries noticed the changes in Shang Feifan. Only A-Dai shrank even closer into Hu Bushuai's embrace.

"What happened to Frank?"

An officer attempted to enter the room, but was blocked by Shang Feifan.

The officer was about to flare up in anger.

Shang Feifan stated coldly, "Rushing in to tamper with the crime scene? Wait outside!"

Intimidated by Old Shang's overwhelming aura, the officers could only watch helplessly as Shang Feifan and Hu Bushuai entered the private room.

"Don't do anything rash. Frank's death is not simple. Let those two go in; it's best we don't get ourselves mixed up in this," the experienced veteran security officer lowered his voice to warn the others.

As soon as these words were spoken, the previously indignant officers fell silent as well.

The moment they stepped into the cell, Shang Feifan and Hu Bushuai exchanged glances.

Things were beginning to distort and escalate.

If poisoning the giant insect mounts was merely meant to be disgusting, and subsequently poisoning the rest area supervisor to frame someone was a display of aristocratic arrogance—the implication being *I did it, but what can you do about it?*—

Then when Frank, the security officer bought off by the mastermind, was also poisoned to death, the situation ceased to be so simple.

It wasn't that the mastermind couldn't do it, but rather that it wasn't worth the trouble—unless this was truly just a prank targeting Hu Bushuai.

Frank lay flat on his back, eyes wide open, dying with grievances unredressed. Aside from the blood flowing from his nose and mouth, his hand loosely gripped a bottle, its cap open, with the majority of the poison inside already spilled out.

On the surface, this looked like yet another suicide scene.

However, the source of the curse did not originate from Frank. Far from it; he was merely a sacrifice—a life offered up to ensure the curse's success.

Shang Feifan saw thick, resentful, and frantic malice swirling around Frank.

This time, however, he did not actively absorb it, instead allowing those wisps of malice to slowly and voluntarily seep into his body.

The malice-absorption progress bar within his right-eye vision popped up once more, ticking upward at a similarly steady pace.

Shang Feifan had no idea what purpose this progress bar served; it seemed merely to indicate how much malice had been absorbed.

What kind of change would occur if the progress bar reached full capacity?

*Ding-dong.*

The system notified him that he had completed Quest Fifty-One, rewarding him with 5 Contribution Points.

Immediately following that, the system issued a new quest.

[Quest Fifty-Two: A suspected suicide case has occurred in the Molo City Sixth District Security Office. Please investigate whether the deceased, Frank, died by suicide. Providing a judgment will reward 1 Contribution Point.]

This quest was relatively easy to complete; he could render a verdict immediately. Before that, however, Shang Feifan looked toward Hu Bushuai.

Hu Bushuai was lowering his gaze, listening intently.

"Secure the scene! No one is allowed to enter!" Inspector Wen's stern shout rang out as he personally rushed to the scene.

The security officers crowded around the cell entrance dispersed.

Inspector Wen paused briefly at the threshold before stepping into the room.

He had a headache!

The identity of this deceased Frank was far from simple.

He was one of the followers of Zhi Gui, the eldest son of Baron Zhipang. A year ago, he had come to work at the security bureau carrying a recommendation letter from Baron Zhipang. Because he never concealed his connection to Baron Zhipang—even boasting about it—the security officers in this district were all well aware of his background.

Until his dying breath, Frank had indeed been running errands for Zhi Gui.

Having heard earlier that the investigator from the upper echelons had actually arrested Frank and suspected him of poisoning the potion market rest area supervisor to frame someone, he had felt a premonition of disaster in his heart.

Never did he expect an even more disastrous turn of events: Frank had actually died right here inside their own office premises.

Right now, he only prayed this matter had nothing to do with Zhi Gui, and even less to do with Baron Zhipang.

"Suicide out of fear of crime?" Inspector Wen had worked frontline cases before; sweeping his gaze across Frank's death scene, he made a preliminary assessment.

With a hint of sarcastic amusement, Shang Feifan smiled. "Are you that eager to close the case this way?"

Tightening his lips, Inspector Wen tried his best to maintain his dignity as an inspector. "Please watch your phrasing, Mr. Hochschild. Our ranks are equal."

He was a Third-Class Inspector, which theoretically put him on par with a Third-Class Investigator.

That was only in theory, however. In practice, investigators from the Special Investigation Bureau always held half a rank higher than local officials, and if they carried confidential orders, their authority was even more formidable.

This was precisely why Inspector Wen had remained so polite to Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan found it amusing; he had no intention whatsoever of suppressing Inspector Wen, yet the man clearly viewed him as an enemy—or if not an enemy, at least a troublemaker.

At that exact moment, Hu Bushuai raised his head and shook it at Shang Feifan. "It wasn't suicide. Someone coerced him, and the poison was also handed to him by that person."

Hearing this, Inspector Wen immediately demanded, "How do you know? What did you discover?"

Hu Bushuai replied indifferently, "My innate talent allows me to hear the lingering murmurs left behind by the deceased after death. Normally, these murmurs also represent the clearest and most deeply etched memories of the dead."

"So you cannot provide concrete evidence," Inspector Wen said with a stern expression.

Hu Bushuai remained unfazed. "I am only responsible for stating my judgment. Finding the true cause of the deceased's death and the mastermind behind it is the job of you security officers."

Inspector Wen gazed deeply at Hu Bushuai, thinking that this person's ability would certainly be immensely useful for investigating cases—what a pity he wasn't his subordinate.

Inspector Wen assumed Hu Bushuai was also personnel from the Special Investigation Bureau, or perhaps someone hired by Shang Feifan to assist. He leaned toward the latter, as no investigator out on a case would drag a small cub along unless that cub possessed extraordinarily special abilities.

"This is a case of staged suicide," Shang Feifan stated his judgment to the system.

In Inspector Wen's ears, however, these words were taken as being spoken directly to him.

"This is not some private detective agency of ours, nor some ignorant village where whatever a priest says goes. Regardless of any conclusions, they must be backed by evidence."

Dropping this resounding statement, Inspector Wen immediately turned and ordered the investigative onlookers at the door, "Have the technical personnel from the forensics department arrive immediately! Furthermore, this case will be personally handled by Pate."

"Understood." The veteran security officer whose name was called walked out with an unchanged expression, though he was actually filled with bitterness.

Shang Feifan took Hu Bushuai's hand, stepped back two paces, and adopted an attitude indicating they had no intention of meddling further in the investigation.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第44章 诅咒直线和郁闷的谷主 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
就在刚刚，系统认可了他的判断，宣布任务五十二完成，1点贡献点到账。

【任务五十三，请找到逼死治安员弗兰克的幕后凶手，并找到药剂市场巨虫坐骑被毒杀案件的幕后真相。成功后奖励10点。】

商非凡挑眉，脑载系统极少发布奖励高达10点以上的任务，能奖励5点都算丰厚。

相对于丰厚的奖励来说，也证明这个任务五十三会比较困难，更可能是推动游戏情节发展的重要线索。

“我们走。”商非凡对虎不帅低语。

虎不帅也低声问：“你不去看证据了吗？”

“没必要了。”商非凡已经抓住了更重要的线索，与其在这里浪费时间，还不如先去找到那个对他下诅咒的人。

商非凡九成肯定，对他下诅咒的人就是逼弗兰克自杀的人。

对方应该一直在监视弗兰克，也可能是在监视其他人，当他发现弗兰克有可能暴露的时候，立刻就献祭了弗兰克。这样既能达到灭口的目的，还能坑他一波。

就是对方为什么会诅咒他？

就因为他抓住了弗兰克？

商非凡翻找记忆，想要找到可疑者。

他抓住弗兰克，再让治安员把弗兰克带回治安办公楼，整个过程见到的人并不多。

他的记忆不错，但他把记忆翻完一遍，也没有找到表现异常的人。

商非凡心想：那个诅咒者要么特别老练，要么就是他有特殊的隐藏方法。幸好他有一根线头系着对方。

文督查听说这两人要离开，差点击鼓相送。他巴不得这两个麻烦赶紧离开。

等他们走了，这个案子想要怎么结，还不是随他。

文督查不是不想把案情调查清楚，他只是不想被牵扯到更复杂的事件当中。

商非凡和虎不帅离开治安办公楼，途径药剂市场休息区，虎不帅被人拦住，对方通知他，他的巨虫坐骑尸体马上就要被焚烧。

“我需要送它一程。”虎不帅把阿呆交还给商非凡。

商非凡接过缩成一团的阿呆，“我陪你一起。”

诅咒之线没断，他就不怕那人跑掉。

虎不帅想要拒绝：“你不是要找幕后凶手吗？我这边可能还要耽误一点时间，要么你先去忙？”

商非凡心中感到一丝怪异，虎不帅明显也想找到幕后凶手，却有意无意想要和他分开行动，难道对方掌握了某个他不知道的线索，还是虎不帅要做某些事不想让他看到？

很好，虎不帅同志，你引起了我更大的兴趣。

“你肚子饿不饿？这都下午了，你中饭还没吃吧，我也没吃。这样，你去送你的巨虫坐骑，我去买点吃的，等会儿去找你。”商非凡特别好脾气地说。

虎不帅张口。

商非凡迅速：“我很饿，阿呆也饿了。我们反正要吃饭，就顺便给你带点吃的。”

虎不帅无奈：“谢谢。”

商非凡对他笑笑，真的去买食物了。

阿呆仰头看他。

商非凡低头，揉揉阿呆的方脑袋：“他很好看对吗。”

阿呆：？

商非凡笑，脚步加快。

阿呆仰头看着笑得十分愉快的老商，身体逐渐放松。

同一时间，千里之外的天残谷玩家营地。

白金色长发垂地的俊美谷主面色忧愁还带着一丝不解，垂眸坐在一口小小的水池边。

两个月前他发布了探查地缝附近那个强盗窝的任务。

领取任务的玩家死了一批又一批，有的死在路上，有的被强盗杀死。

最幸运也最倒霉的那个，逃出了强盗窝，却又莫名其妙地被杀死。

谷主知道那个传说，但当时他完全没想到那个玩家的死亡会和那个恐怖传说有关。

直到他派出的又一支玩家队伍成功抵达强盗窝，却发现强盗窝中的强盗都消失了。

只是强盗消失还没什么，可关键是强盗窝的库房也空了！

好在他最想要的那个东西还在，只是不在强盗窝中。

那个东西一直在移动，他有心派玩家跟上去，但那些玩家等级太低，让他们现在就踏入荒野，就是让他们送死。

玩家死亡，就得重生。

重生就要消耗能量给玩家重新生成一具身体。

如果不是重新生成一具身体耗费能量太多，他又怎么会做出死亡就要下线七十二小时的惩罚？

计算了下要消耗的成本，他不得不暂时按下这个任务，先把全部精力都用在营地建设上。

建设营地，就是为了给玩家建设安全上下线的安全区。

有了安全区为立脚点，玩家才能一点点稳步前进向外拓展。

否则玩家死一次就要从出生点跑好几天甚至是更长时间去往任务地点，就算这个游戏有全息的名头，也会让玩家拒玩。

可就在今天，就在刚刚，他发现那个东西的指引消失了！

这说明那东西不是被摧毁，就是被谁给吸收使用。

俊美的谷主……十分憋屈。

他谋算了那么久！

如果不是他身体情况特殊，如果不是他也需要依托营地才能行动自如，他怎么可能放过就在家门口的宝贝！

原本他计划得好好的，先让玩家摸底，再在那强盗窝附近建设三号玩家营地，等营地完工，他就能率领上万名玩家去推平那个强盗窝，从而得到那个宝贝。

顺便还能利用强盗窝的粮食库存来弥补一下玩家数量增长过快导致的口粮危机。

是的！就因为粮食不够，他甚至不能放出太多游戏账号，让更多玩家进入游戏。

毕竟，这是一个真实的世界，就算玩家的身体都是特别生成，可在去除掉活尸啃食活物的特性后，总得给他们其他补充能量的渠道。

这个渠道就是通过食用正常食物来获取能量。

如此一来，粮食就是重中之重！

人口代表劳动力没错，但也需要时间来完成良性循环。

就算是植物生长系异能，也要考虑到植物种子的数量、土地养分消耗等实际问题。

更不要说想要培养一个能让植物快速生长的植物异能者，还得看玩家的血脉天赋，更要看那个玩家愿不愿意付出大量时间和精力来提升自己的异能。

如果这真的是游戏就好了。

俊美的谷主在心中叹息。

算了，那宝贝没了就没了，他还有其他目标。

等他获得剩下的八份虫母心脏碎片，再去把那个好运的家伙给吸收掉就是。

就是那个强盗窝的突发事件打乱了他很多初期布局，导致他不得不临时更改计划。

但谁能想到那个传说中的恐怖玩意会突然冒出来？

谷主想不通原因，只能当自己这一波运气不太好。

“谷主，您找我？”一名玩家大步流星地走近水池。

谷主抬头，蓝紫色的眼眸看人时自带深情魅惑力，“你来了。听说你所属的队伍是我们这里最强的一支佣兵小队，我有一个重要任务要交给你们小队。”

伏向军拍拍胸膛：“您说，保证完成任务！”
chunks.englishText:
Just a moment ago, the system had acknowledged his judgment, announcing the completion of Quest Fifty-Two, with 1 contribution point credited to his account.

【Quest Fifty-Three: Please find the mastermind behind the murder that forced Investigator Frank to his death, and uncover the true culprit behind the poisoning of the giant worm mount in the potion market. Reward: 10 points upon success.】

Shang Feifan raised an eyebrow. The onboard system rarely issued quests with rewards as high as 10 points or more; getting even 5 points was considered quite generous.

In contrast to the generous reward, this also proved that Quest Fifty-Three would be rather difficult, and more likely an important clue driving the progression of the game's plot.

"Let's go," Shang Feifan whispered to Hu Bushuai.

Hu Bushuai also asked in a low voice, "Aren't you going to look at the evidence?"

"No need." Shang Feifan had already grasped a more important clue. Rather than wasting time here, it was better to first go find the person who had placed a curse on him.

Shang Feifan was ninety percent certain that the person who cursed him was the exact same person who had forced Frank to commit suicide.

That individual must have been monitoring Frank the entire time—or perhaps monitoring others as well. When he realized that Frank was at risk of being exposed, he immediately sacrificed Frank. This achieved the goal of silencing him while simultaneously framing Shang Feifan.

The only question was: why would the other party place a curse on him?

Just because he had captured Frank?

Shang Feifan rummaged through his memories, searching for suspicious individuals.

The entire process—from capturing Frank to having the investigators escort him back to the investigation office—had involved very few people.

His memory was quite good, but after reviewing every single detail, he couldn't find anyone who had acted abnormally.

Shang Feifan thought to himself: That curse-caster is either extremely seasoned or possesses some special concealment method. Fortunately, he still had a thread tethering him to the other party.

Upon hearing that these two troublemakers were finally leaving, Inspector Wen was so relieved he could have beaten a drum to send them off. He was more than eager for them to scram as fast as possible.

Once they were gone, how this case would be closed was entirely up to him.

It wasn't that Inspector Wen didn't want to investigate the case thoroughly; he simply didn't want to be dragged into an even more complicated mess.

Shang Feifan and Hu Bushuai left the investigation office. As they passed the rest area of the potion market, Hu Bushuai was intercepted by someone who informed him that the corpse of his giant worm mount was about to be cremated.

"I need to see it off on its final journey," Hu Bushuai said, handing Ah Dai back to Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan took the curled-up Ah Dai, "I'll go with you."

As long as the cursed thread remained unbroken, he wasn't afraid of that person running away.

Hu Bushuai wanted to refuse: "Don't you need to find the mastermind? Things might take a while on my end, so why don't you go take care of your business first?"

A trace of strangeness arose in Shang Feifan's heart. Hu Bushuai clearly wanted to find the mastermind as well, yet he kept intentionally or unintentionally trying to separate from him. Could it be that the fellow had grasped some clue unknown to him, or was there something Hu Bushuai wanted to do without him seeing?

Very well, Comrade Hu Bushuai, you've sparked an even greater interest in me.

"Aren't you hungry? It's already the afternoon, you haven't had lunch yet, right? Neither have I. How about this: you go send off your giant worm mount, and I'll go buy some food. I'll come find you later," Shang Feifan said with extreme amiability.

Hu Bushuai opened his mouth to speak.

Shang Feifan quickly added, "I'm very hungry, and Ah Dai is hungry too. Since we have to eat anyway, I'll just pick up some food for you along the way."

Hu Bushuai sighed helplessly, "Thank you."

Shang Feifan smiled at him and genuinely went off to buy food.

Ah Dai looked up at him.

Shang Feifan lowered his head and rubbed Ah Dai's square head, "He's very good-looking, isn't he?"

Ah Dai: ?

Shang Feifan chuckled, quickening his pace.

Looking up at Old Shang, who was smiling quite happily, Ah Dai gradually relaxed his body.

At the same time, thousands of miles away in the Skyshatter Valley (Tianchan Gu) player camp.

The handsome valley master, whose platinum-gold long hair trailed all the way to the ground, wore a worried expression tinged with a hint of incomprehension as he lowered his gaze and sat by the edge of a small pond.

Two months ago, he had released a quest to investigate the bandit lair near the earth fissure.

Batches after batch of players who accepted the quest had died; some perished on the road, while others were killed by the bandits.

The luckiest—and yet most unlucky—one had managed to escape the bandit lair, only to be inexplicably killed off.

The valley master knew of that legend, but at the time, he never expected that the player's death would be connected to that terrifying myth.

It wasn't until another team of players he dispatched successfully reached the bandit lair that they discovered the bandits inside had completely vanished.

The bandits disappearing was one thing, but the crucial point was that the bandit lair's storehouse had also been cleaned out!

Fortunately, the exact item he desired most was still there—though it was no longer inside the bandit lair.

That item had been constantly moving. He had the mind to send players to follow it, but those players were too low-leveled; letting them venture into the wilderness right now would be sending them to their deaths.

When players died, they had to respawn.

Respawning required expending energy to regenerate a physical body for the player.

If regenerating a physical body didn't consume so much energy, why would he have instituted a penalty where death resulted in being logged off for seventy-two hours?

Calculating the costs involved, he had no choice but to temporarily shelve this quest and focus all his energy on camp construction.

Building the camp was meant to establish a safe zone where players could safely log in and out.

With the safe zone as a foothold, the players could step-by-step and steadily expand outward.

Otherwise, if players died once only to have to run for days or even longer from the spawn point to the quest location, even with the gimmick of full immersion, players would quit the game.

Yet today, just moments ago, he discovered that the guidance of that item had vanished!

This meant the item had either been destroyed or absorbed and used by someone.

The handsome valley master... felt utterly aggrieved.

He had plotted for so long!

If not for his special physical condition, and if not for the fact that he also needed to rely on the camp to move about freely, how could he possibly have let go of a treasure sitting right on his doorstep?

Originally, his plan had been well-laid: first, have the players scout the area, then build the No. 3 player camp near the bandit lair. Once the camp was completed, he would lead tens of thousands of players to flatten that bandit lair and thus acquire the treasure.

Along the way, he could also use the bandit lair's food reserves to alleviate the food crisis caused by the rapid growth in the player population.

Yes! Precisely because of insufficient food supplies, he hadn't even dared to release too many game accounts to let more players enter the game.

After all, this was a real world. Even though the players' bodies were specially generated, once you stripped away the living corpses' trait of devouring living beings, you still had to provide them with other channels to replenish their energy.

That channel was acquiring energy by consuming normal food.

Consequently, food was of paramount importance!

Population represented labor force, true, but it also required time to complete a virtuous cycle.

Even with plant-growth-type supernatural abilities, one still had to account for practical issues such as the quantity of plant seeds and the consumption of soil nutrients.

Not to mention that nurturing a plant esper capable of rapid plant growth depended on the player's bloodline talent, as well as whether that player was willing to invest a massive amount of time and energy to enhance their ability.

If only this really were a game.

The handsome valley master sighed inwardly.

Forget it, if that treasure was gone, it was gone; he still had other targets.

Once he acquired the remaining eight fragments of the broodmother's heart, he would simply go absorb that lucky fellow.

It was just that the unexpected incident at the bandit lair had disrupted many of his initial layouts, forcing him to temporarily alter his plans.

Yet who could have predicted that legendary terrifying entity would suddenly pop out of nowhere?

Unable to figure out the reason, the valley master could only chalk it up to having rather poor luck this time around.

"Valley Master, you were looking for me?" A player strode up to the edge of the pond.

The valley master raised his head, his blue-purple eyes carrying an innate, alluring depth when gazing at someone. "You've arrived. I heard that the squad you belong to is our strongest mercenary team. I have an important mission to entrust to your team."

Fu Xiangjun patted his chest. "Just name it, guaranteed completion!"
